Prevent air supply and deploy the fire extinguisher with short, economical bursts, fighting the fire from above as much as possible.
Read the operating instructions and deploy the fire extinguisher immediately, fighting the fire from below as much as possible.

explanation.de: Um einen Brand wirksam zu bekämpfen, muss zunächst die Luftzufuhr unterbunden werden (z. B. Fenster und Luken schließen), damit das Feuer keinen Sauerstoff nachbekommt. Der Feuerlöscher soll erst direkt am Brandherd eingesetzt werden und das Feuer von unten bekämpft werden, da Löschmittel so unter die Flammen gelangen und die Brennstoffoberfläche bedecken. Option b ist falsch, weil das Richten des Strahls in die lodernden Flammen das Löschmittel vergeudet; Option c ist falsch, weil das Bekämpfen von oben weniger wirksam ist.
explanation.en: To fight a fire effectively, the air supply must first be cut off (e.g. closing hatches and ports) to deprive the fire of oxygen. The extinguisher should only be deployed directly at the seat of the fire, attacking from below so the agent reaches under the flames and covers the fuel surface. Option b is incorrect because directing the jet into open flames wastes the extinguishing agent; option c is incorrect because attacking from above is less effective.
explanation.memoryAid: Low and close: cut the air, aim at the base — starve the fire from the bottom up.

en.question: How must one behave after a collision?
answers: Render assistance and remain at the scene of the accident until further assistance is no longer required; exchange all necessary details.
Render assistance and remain at the scene of the accident until further assistance is no longer required; notify the water police.
Render assistance and remain at the scene of the accident until further assistance is no longer required; give a distress signal.
Render assistance and remain at the scene of the accident until further assistance is no longer required; establish watertight integrity.

explanation.de: Nach einem Zusammenstoß ist man verpflichtet, Hilfe zu leisten, am Unfallort zu bleiben, bis keine weitere Hilfe nötig ist, und alle erforderlichen Daten (z. B. Name, Schiff, Versicherung) auszutauschen. Die Wasserschutzpolizei zu benachrichtigen ist nicht zwingend vorgeschrieben, ein Notsignal ist nur bei akuter Not erforderlich, und das Herstellen des Verschlusszustands ist eine separate Sicherheitsmaßnahme, aber keine eigenständige gesetzliche Nachunfallpflicht.
explanation.en: After a collision, one is legally obliged to render assistance, remain on scene until no further help is needed, and exchange all necessary details (e.g. name, vessel, insurance). Notifying the water police is not a mandatory post-collision duty, a distress signal is only required in cases of acute distress, and establishing watertight integrity is a separate safety measure rather than a standalone legal post-accident obligation.
explanation.memoryAid: Collide → Stay & Exchange: stay on scene, swap details.

en.question: What factors are primarily responsible for weather events, i.e. wind and precipitation?
answers: Changes in air pressure, humidity, and temperature.
Changes in air pressure, solar radiation, and altitude.
Changes in air pressure, humidity, and season.
Changes in air pressure, time of day, and temperature.

explanation.de: Wind und Niederschlag werden hauptsächlich durch Luftdruckänderungen, Luftfeuchtigkeit und Temperatur bestimmt. Die Luftfeuchtigkeit entscheidet über Kondensation und Niederschlag, während die Temperatur die Luftdichte und damit die Druckgefälle beeinflusst, die Wind verursachen. Jahreszeit und Tageszeit sind sekundäre Einflussgrößen.
explanation.en: Wind and precipitation are primarily driven by changes in air pressure, atmospheric humidity, and temperature. Humidity determines whether condensation and precipitation occur, while temperature influences air density and therefore pressure gradients that cause wind. Season and time of day are secondary influences, and altitude and solar radiation, while relevant, are not the primary trio for weather events.
explanation.memoryAid: **P-H-T**: Pressure changes, Humidity, Temperature — the weather trinity.

en.question: In which situation may distress signals be used?
answers: When there is danger to the life or limb of persons and assistance is therefore required.
When there is danger to the life or limb of persons or the vessel can no longer be safely manoeuvred.
When there is danger to the life or limb of persons or significant property values and assistance is therefore required.
When there is danger to the life or limb of persons, significant property values, or the maritime environment.

explanation.de: Notsignale dürfen ausschließlich dann gegeben werden, wenn tatsächlich Gefahr für Leib oder Leben von Personen besteht und deshalb Hilfe benötigt wird. Sachschäden oder Manövrierunfähigkeit allein rechtfertigen keinen Notruf — das würde den Missbrauch von Notsignalen darstellen und ist strafbar.
explanation.en: Distress signals may only be used when there is a genuine danger to the life or limb of persons and assistance is required. Property damage or loss of manoeuvrability alone do not justify a distress call — misuse of distress signals is a punishable offence.
explanation.memoryAid: Distress = people in danger needing help — not ships, not cargo.

en.question: Where do the Collision Regulations (COLREGs) apply?
answers: On the high seas and in all waters connected therewith that are navigable by seagoing vessels.
On the high seas and the German sea waterways (Seeschifffahrtsstraßen) navigated by seagoing vessels.
On the sea waterways (Seeschifffahrtsstraßen) and the coastal German sea waters navigated by seagoing vessels.
On the high seas and the marginal seas navigable by seagoing vessels, with the exception of traffic separation schemes.

explanation.de: Die KVR gelten auf der Hohen See und allen damit zusammenhängenden, von Seeschiffen befahrbaren Gewässern — so legt es Regel 1(a) der KVR fest. Antwort (b) ist zu eng, da sie die Geltung auf deutsche Seeschifffahrtsstraßen beschränkt, und (d) ist falsch, weil Verkehrstrennungsgebiete ausdrücklich von den KVR erfasst werden, nicht ausgenommen sind.
explanation.en: The COLREGs apply on the high seas and in all waters connected to it that are navigable by seagoing vessels — this is the scope defined in COLREG Rule 1(a). Answer (b) is too narrow because it limits application to German sea waterways only, and (d) is wrong because traffic separation schemes are explicitly covered by the COLREGs, not excluded.
explanation.memoryAid: COLREGs follow the sea: wherever a seagoing vessel can sail from the high seas, the rules sail with it.

en.question: What applies when a provision of the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO) conflicts with the Collision Regulations (COLREGs)?
answers: The provision of the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO).
The provision of the Collision Regulations (COLREGs).
The basic rules of conduct in traffic.
The provision of the Schifffahrtsordnung Emsmündung (Ems Estuary Navigation Order).

explanation.de: Gemäß der SeeSchStrO gilt: Steht eine ihrer Bestimmungen im Widerspruch zu den KVR, so geht die SeeSchStrO als speziellere nationale Regelung vor. Die KVR (COLREG) erlauben ausdrücklich, dass Küstenstaaten für Binnenwasserstraßen und spezielle Gewässer abweichende Regelungen treffen dürfen. Die Antworten b, c und d sind falsch, da weder die KVR noch allgemeine Grundregeln noch die Schifffahrtsordnung Emsmündung in diesem Verhältnis Vorrang haben.
explanation.en: When a provision of the SeeSchStrO conflicts with the COLREGs, the SeeSchStrO takes precedence as the more specific national regulation. The COLREGs explicitly permit coastal states to adopt special rules for their inland waterways and specific waters. Answers b, c, and d are incorrect because neither the COLREGs, general rules of conduct, nor the Ems Estuary Navigation Order take precedence in this relationship.
explanation.memoryAid: Special local law beats general international rule — SeeSchStrO is 'lex specialis' on German waters.

en.question: Which recreational boats are exempt from the licence requirement on sea waterways (Seeschifffahrtsstraßen)?
answers: Recreational boats without a propulsion engine, or those with a maximum non-exceedable rated power of 11.03 kilowatts (15 hp) when using an internal combustion engine, or 7.5 kilowatts when using an electric motor in operating mode S1 (continuous duty) or less.
Sailing recreational boats with a hull length of less than 20 m and those whose propulsion engine is not in use.

Recreational boats with a propulsion engine with a rated power greater than 11.03 kilowatts (15 hp) when using an internal combustion engine, or greater than 7.5 kilowatts when using an electric motor in operating mode S1 (continuous duty).
Recreational boats that are either at anchor, made fast to the shore, or aground.

explanation.de: Auf den Seeschifffahrtsstraßen besteht Fahrerlaubnispflicht nur für Sportboote, deren Antriebsmaschine eine Nutzleistung von mehr als 11,03 kW (15 PS) bei Verbrennungsmotoren bzw. mehr als 7,5 kW (Elektromotor, Dauerbetrieb S1) hat. Boote ohne Motor oder unterhalb dieser Leistungsgrenzen sind ausgenommen. Antwort b ist falsch, weil allein das Nichtbenutzen des Motors keine Ausnahme begründet; Antwort d ist irrelevant, da ankernde oder festgemachte Boote keine Fahrt machen.
explanation.en: On sea waterways (Seeschifffahrtsstraßen), a licence is only required for recreational boats whose engine exceeds 11.03 kW (15 hp) for combustion engines or 7.5 kW for electric motors in continuous-duty mode S1. Boats with no engine or below these power thresholds are exempt. Answer b is incorrect because simply not using the engine does not create an exemption; answer d is irrelevant since anchored or moored boats are not underway.
explanation.memoryAid: 15 hp / 11 kW combustion, 7.5 kW electric — stay below these limits and no licence is needed at sea.

en.question: Who is responsible for complying with the traffic regulations?
answers: The skipper or his deputy.
The skipper and his deputy.
The skipper and any other person responsible.
The skipper or any other person responsible.

explanation.de: Die Verantwortung für die Einhaltung der Verkehrsvorschriften liegt beim Fahrzeugführer oder, wenn dieser nicht selbst das Steuer führt, bei seinem benannten Stellvertreter. Es handelt sich um eine Entweder-oder-Verantwortung (jeweils eine Person), nicht um eine gemeinsame Verantwortung aller Beteiligten an Bord.
explanation.en: Responsibility for complying with traffic regulations rests with the skipper, or — when the skipper is not personally at the helm — his designated deputy. It is an either/or assignment of responsibility (one person in charge at any given time), not a joint responsibility shared among all parties on board.
explanation.memoryAid: One helm, one boss — the skipper OR their stand-in, never a committee.

en.question: What does 'seamanlike duty of care' (seemännische Sorgfaltspflicht) mean?
answers: The obligation to observe precautionary measures beyond the traffic regulations, as required by seamanship practice or the special circumstances of the case.

The obligation to observe the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO), the Collision Regulations (COLREGs), the general rules of conduct in traffic, and the rules of giving way including the last-moment manoeuvre.
The obligation to observe the precautionary and safety rules of the traffic regulations and the general rules of conduct in traffic.
The obligation to observe the precautionary measures of the Collision Regulations (COLREGs), the general rules of conduct in traffic, and the rules of giving way including the last-moment manoeuvre.

explanation.de: Die seemännische Sorgfaltspflicht geht über die bloße Einhaltung der geschriebenen Verkehrsvorschriften hinaus: Sie verlangt zusätzliche Vorsicht, die der Seemannsbrauch oder besondere Umstände erfordern. Antwort b, c und d beschreiben lediglich die Pflicht zur Einhaltung bestimmter Vorschriften, erfassen aber nicht diesen weitergehenden Gedanken des guten Seemannsbrauchs.
explanation.en: The seamanlike duty of care goes beyond mere compliance with written traffic regulations: it demands additional precautions required by good seamanship practice or the special circumstances of the situation. Options b, c, and d only describe the duty to comply with specific regulations and therefore miss this broader concept of good seamanship.
explanation.memoryAid: Good seamanship = rules PLUS whatever the sea demands — always go the extra mile.

en.question: What safety measures must the skipper take, as part of their duty of seamanlike care, before departure, to protect and ensure the safety of persons on board?
answers: The skipper must brief all crew members and guests on the safety precautions on board, instruct them in the use of life-saving and firefighting equipment, and advise them on appropriate measures to prevent falling overboard, as well as informing them that wearing a lifejacket at all times increases survival chances in the water.

The skipper must instruct all crew members and guests to inform themselves about the safety precautions on board, to read the operating instructions for the life-saving and firefighting equipment, and to observe appropriate measures to prevent falling overboard, as well as informing them that wearing a lifejacket at all times increases survival chances in the water.

The skipper must brief the responsible crew members on the safety precautions on board, instruct them in the use of life-saving and firefighting equipment, and advise them on appropriate measures to prevent falling overboard, as well as informing them that wearing a lifejacket at all times increases survival chances in the water.

The skipper must brief the guests on board on the safety precautions on board, instruct them in the use of life-saving and firefighting equipment, and advise them on appropriate measures to prevent falling overboard, as well as informing them that wearing a lifejacket at all times increases survival chances in the water.

explanation.de: Die korrekte Antwort (a) verlangt, dass der Fahrzeugführer sowohl Besatzungsmitglieder als auch Gäste aktiv unterrichtet und einweist — nicht nur die 'verantwortlichen' Besatzungsmitglieder (c) und nicht nur die Gäste (d). Antwort (b) ist falsch, weil der Fahrzeugführer die Pflicht hat, die Einweisung selbst aktiv durchzuführen, und diese Verantwortung nicht an die Personen delegieren darf, sich selbst zu informieren.
explanation.en: The correct answer (a) requires the skipper to actively brief and instruct both crew members and guests — not only the 'responsible' crew members (c) and not only the guests (d). Answer (b) is incorrect because the skipper has a duty to actively carry out the safety briefing personally and cannot delegate this responsibility by merely telling people to read the instructions themselves.
explanation.memoryAid: The skipper briefs EVERYONE — crew AND guests — not just some, and does it actively, not by handing out manuals.

en.question: What does the 'last moment manoeuvre' mean?
answers: An evasive manoeuvre by the stand-on vessel.
An evasive manoeuvre by the give-way vessel.
An evasive manoeuvre by both the stand-on vessel and the give-way vessel.
An evasive manoeuvre by either the stand-on vessel or the give-way vessel.

explanation.de: Das 'Manöver des letzten Augenblicks' (Regel 17 KVR) bezeichnet das Ausweichmanöver des Kurshalters, wenn ein Zusammenstoß nicht mehr allein durch den Ausweichpflichtigen abgewendet werden kann. Der Kurshalter hält normalerweise Kurs und Geschwindigkeit, darf aber — und muss letztlich — manövrieren, wenn der Ausweichpflichtige nicht handelt. Das Manöver des Ausweichpflichtigen findet früher statt und ist daher nicht das 'Manöver des letzten Augenblicks'.
explanation.en: The 'last moment manoeuvre' (COLREG Rule 17) refers specifically to an evasive action taken by the stand-on vessel (Kurshalter) when a collision can no longer be avoided by the give-way vessel alone. The stand-on vessel normally maintains course and speed, but is permitted — and ultimately required — to manoeuvre if the give-way vessel fails to act. The give-way vessel (Ausweichpflichtiger) has the primary obligation to avoid collision and acts earlier, so its manoeuvre is not the 'last moment' manoeuvre.
explanation.memoryAid: The STAND-ON vessel gets the LAST word — if the give-way vessel doesn't act, the stand-on vessel must act at the last moment.

en.question: When must the "last moment manoeuvre" be carried out?
answers: It must be carried out when a collision can no longer be avoided by the manoeuvres of the give-way vessel alone.
It must be carried out when a collision can no longer be avoided by the manoeuvres of the stand-on vessel alone.
It must be carried out at the last moment by every vessel when a collision can otherwise no longer be avoided.
It must be carried out shortly before the collision when a collision can otherwise no longer be avoided by the manoeuvres of the stand-on vessel alone.

explanation.de: Das "Manöver des letzten Augenblicks" (COLREG Regel 17) wird von dem Kurshalter (und ggf. allen Beteiligten) durchgeführt, sobald der Ausweichpflichtige allein die Kollision nicht mehr abwenden kann. Entscheidend ist, dass es nicht auf den Kurshalter allein beschränkt ist (wie Antwort b und d suggerieren), sondern ausgelöst wird, wenn das Ausweichmanöver des Ausweichpflichtigen allein nicht mehr ausreicht.
explanation.en: The "last moment manoeuvre" (COLREG Rule 17) becomes obligatory when the give-way vessel's actions alone are no longer sufficient to prevent a collision — at that point the stand-on vessel (and any other vessel involved) must also act. Answer b is wrong because it incorrectly names the stand-on vessel as the trigger; answer d conflates the trigger condition with the stand-on vessel's sole responsibility.
explanation.memoryAid: Give-way vessel fails → stand-on vessel must not wait: last moment manoeuvre kicks in.

en.question: When is a vessel considered an overtaking vessel?
answers: When it is approaching another vessel from a direction more than 22.5° abaft the beam (the sector of the sternlight).
When it is approaching another vessel from a direction more than 112.5° abaft the beam (the sector of the sidelights).
When it is positioned relative to another vessel at a direction more than 22.5° abaft the beam (the sector of the sternlight).
When it passes another vessel coming from an astern direction more than 22.5° forward of the beam (the sector of the masthead light).

explanation.de: Ein Fahrzeug gilt als überholendes Fahrzeug, wenn es sich einem anderen Fahrzeug aus einer Richtung von mehr als 22,5° achterlicher als querab nähert – also aus dem Bereich, der vom Hecklicht (135°, aufgeteilt in je 67,5° je Seite) abgedeckt wird (KVR Regel 13). Entscheidend ist das aktive Nähern, nicht bloß die momentane Position (Unterschied zu Antwort c). Antwort b nennt mit 112,5° fälschlicherweise den Bereich der Seitenlichter.
explanation.en: A vessel is considered overtaking when it is approaching another vessel from a direction more than 22.5° abaft the beam — the arc covered by the sternlight (135°, i.e. 67.5° on each side) under COLREG Rule 13. The key element is the act of approaching, not merely occupying that bearing (which distinguishes the correct answer from distractor c). Distractor b incorrectly states 112.5°, which corresponds to the sidelights' arc.
explanation.memoryAid: Sternlight = 135° arc = 67.5° each side abaft the beam: if you see only the sternlight, you're the overtaking vessel.

en.question: When is a vessel considered not under command?
answers: When, due to some exceptional circumstance such as failure of the steering or propulsion system, it is unable to manoeuvre as required by the rules and is therefore unable to keep out of the way of another vessel.
When, due to the nature of its work, it is restricted in its ability to manoeuvre as required by the rules and is therefore unable to keep out of the way of another vessel.
When, due to its draught in relation to the available depth and width of navigable water, it is severely restricted in its ability to deviate from the course it is following.
When it is fishing with nets, lines, trawls or other fishing gear that restricts its manoeuvrability.

explanation.de: Ein manövrierunfähiges Fahrzeug (COLREG Regel 3f) ist durch außergewöhnliche Umstände – wie Ruder- oder Maschinenausfall – nicht in der Lage, regelgerecht zu manövrieren. Antwort b beschreibt ein in seiner Manövrierfähigkeit behindertes Fahrzeug (Regel 3g), Antwort c ein tiefgangsbehindertes Fahrzeug (Regel 3h) und Antwort d ein fischendes Fahrzeug (Regel 3i).
explanation.en: A vessel 'not under command' (COLREG Rule 3f) is unable to manoeuvre as required due to an exceptional circumstance such as rudder or engine failure. Answer b describes a vessel 'restricted in her ability to manoeuvre' (Rule 3g), answer c describes a 'vessel constrained by her draught' (Rule 3h), and answer d describes a 'vessel engaged in fishing' (Rule 3i).
explanation.memoryAid: NUC = Not Under Command = something broke — it's an accident, not by design.

en.question: When is a vessel considered to be restricted in her ability to manoeuvre?
answers: When she is impeded by the nature of her work and therefore unable to manoeuvre as required by the rules, and consequently unable to keep out of the way of another vessel.

When, due to exceptional circumstances such as the failure of her steering gear or engine, she is unable to manoeuvre as required by the rules, and consequently unable to keep out of the way of another vessel.
When she is severely restricted in her ability to deviate from her course due to her draught in relation to the available depth and width of navigable water.
When she is fishing with nets, lines, trawls, or other fishing gear that restricts her manoeuvrability.

explanation.de: Ein 'manövrierbehinderte Fahrzeug' (RAM – Restricted in Ability to Manoeuvre) ist laut COLREG Rule 3(g) ein Fahrzeug, das aufgrund der Art seines Einsatzes (z. B. Vermessungsarbeiten, Taucher an Bord, Minenräumen) nicht manövrieren kann. Antwort b) beschreibt ein 'nicht manövrierfähiges Fahrzeug' (NUC – Not Under Command), Antwort c) ein 'tiefgangbehindertes Fahrzeug' und Antwort d) ein 'fischendes Fahrzeug' – allesamt eigene Kategorien nach COLREG.
explanation.en: A 'vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre' (RAM) is defined under COLREG Rule 3(g) as one impeded by the nature of her work (e.g. surveying, diver operations, minesweeping). Answer b) describes a 'vessel not under command' (NUC – e.g. steering failure), answer c) describes a 'vessel constrained by her draught', and answer d) describes a 'vessel engaged in fishing' — all distinct COLREG categories.
explanation.memoryAid: RAM = Restricted by Assignment/Mission (the type of work she is doing).

en.question: What special measures must be taken in restricted visibility?
answers: You must proceed at a safe speed adapted to the reduced visibility conditions, sound signals must be given, navigation lights must be switched on, and a proper lookout must be kept.
You must proceed at a safe speed adapted to the reduced visibility conditions, sound signals must be given, the radar must be switched on, and a lookout must be kept.
You must proceed at a safe speed adapted to the reduced visibility conditions, sound signals must be given, navigation lights must be switched on, and a radar reflector must be deployed.
You must proceed at reduced speed, sound signals must be given, navigation lights must be switched on, and the AIS (Automatic Identification System) must be switched on.

explanation.de: Bei verminderter Sicht schreibt die KVR (COLREG Regel 19) vier Kernmaßnahmen vor: sichere, angepasste Geschwindigkeit, Schallsignale (Nebelsignale), Positionslichter und gehöriger Ausguck. Antwort b lässt die Positionslichter weg; Antwort c ersetzt den Ausguck durch den Radarreflektor (dieser ist zwar sinnvoll, ersetzt aber nicht den Ausguck); Antwort d spricht fälschlicherweise nur von 'verminderter' statt 'angepasster' Geschwindigkeit und nennt AIS statt Ausguck.
explanation.en: In restricted visibility, COLREG Rule 19 requires four core measures: a safe speed adapted to conditions, sound signals (fog signals), navigation lights switched on, and a proper lookout. Answer b omits navigation lights; answer c replaces the lookout with a radar reflector (useful but not a substitute for lookout); answer d incorrectly says only 'reduced speed' rather than 'safe, adapted speed' and lists AIS instead of a proper lookout.
explanation.memoryAid: 4 L's in fog: Lights on, Low-adapted speed, Listen & sound signals, Lookout posted.

en.question: Which regulations govern the equipment, arrangement, and fitting of navigation lights, day shapes, and sound signalling appliances on vessels?
answers: The Collision Regulations (COLREGs), the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO), and the Schifffahrtsordnung Emsmündung (EmsSchO).
The Collision Regulations (COLREGs), the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO), and the Sportbootführerscheinverordnung (recreational boat licence ordinance).
The Collision Regulations (COLREGs), the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO), and the Schiffssicherheitsverordnung (ship safety ordinance).
The Collision Regulations (COLREGs), the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO), and the Verordnung zur Sicherung der Seefahrt (ordinance for the safety of navigation).

explanation.de: Die Ausrüstung, Anordnung und Anbringung von Positionslaternen, Sichtzeichen und Schallsignalanlagen wird durch die KVR (international), die SeeSchStrO (für deutsche Küstengewässer) und ergänzend durch die EmsSchO (für die Emsmündung) geregelt. Die anderen genannten Verordnungen (Sportbootführerscheinverordnung, Schiffssicherheitsverordnung, Verordnung zur Sicherung der Seefahrt) enthalten keine spezifischen Vorschriften zu diesem Thema.
explanation.en: The equipment, arrangement, and fitting of navigation lights, day shapes, and sound signalling appliances are governed by the COLREGs (internationally), the SeeSchStrO (for German coastal waters), and additionally by the EmsSchO (for the Ems estuary area). The other ordinances listed — the recreational boat licence ordinance, the ship safety ordinance, and the navigation safety ordinance — do not contain specific provisions on this subject.
explanation.memoryAid: COLREGs covers the seas, SeeSchStrO covers German coastal waters, and EmsSchO adds the Ems estuary — three layers, three rules.

en.question: Which navigation lights and sound signalling appliances may be used on recreational vessels sailing under the German flag?
answers: Those whose design type has been approved for use by the Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency (BSH), or which hold an equivalent approval recognised by an EU member state.
Those that achieve the required minimum luminous range of three nautical miles, the correct size and colour or sound level, and are accompanied by a certificate from a classification society.
Those that are prescribed in accordance with the Collision Regulations (COLREGs), the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO) and the Schifffahrtsordnung Emsmündung (EmsSchO) and bear a CE mark.
Those that have been tested by the Technischer Überwachungsverein (TÜV) and bear the GS (Geprüfte Sicherheit – tested safety) mark.

explanation.de: Auf Sportbooten unter deutscher Flagge dürfen nur Positionslaternen und Schallsignalanlagen verwendet werden, deren Baumuster vom BSH zugelassen ist oder die eine gleichwertige EU-Zulassung besitzen. Ein CE-Zeichen allein (Antwort c) oder ein TÜV/GS-Zeichen (Antwort d) reicht nicht aus, da diese Kennzeichnungen keine BSH-Typzulassung ersetzen.
explanation.en: Only navigation lights and sound signalling appliances whose design type has been approved by the BSH — or holds an equivalent approval from an EU member state — may be used on recreational vessels flying the German flag. A CE mark alone (answer c) or a TÜV/GS mark (answer d) is not sufficient, as these do not replace BSH type approval.
explanation.memoryAid: BSH stamp = BSH approved: only the official BSH (or EU-equivalent) type approval counts for German-flagged vessels.

en.question: What are "traffic separation schemes"?
answers: These are officially published shipping routes divided into one-way lanes by separation lines or separation zones.
These are officially published fairways divided into one-way lanes by separation lines or separation zones.
These are officially published sea waterways (Seeschifffahrtsstraßen) divided into one-way lanes by separation lines or separation zones.
These are officially published federal waterways (Bundeswasserstraßen) divided into one-way lanes by separation lines or separation zones.

explanation.de: Verkehrstrennungsgebiete (Traffic Separation Schemes, TSS) sind offiziell bekannt gemachte Schifffahrtswege – nicht nur Fahrwasser, Seeschifffahrtsstraßen oder Bundeswasserstraßen – die durch Trennlinien oder Trennzonen in gegenläufige Einbahnspuren aufgeteilt sind. Der Begriff 'Schifffahrtswege' ist der allgemeinste und korrekte Oberbegriff gemäß COLREG Regel 10.
explanation.en: Traffic Separation Schemes (TSS) are officially published shipping routes – not limited to fairways, sea waterways, or federal waterways – divided by separation lines or separation zones into opposing one-way lanes. The term 'shipping routes' (Schifffahrtswege) is the correct, broadest term as used in COLREG Rule 10. The distractors use narrower or more specific categories of waterway that do not capture the full scope of TSS.
explanation.memoryAid: TSS = Traffic lanes Separated by lines/zones on any published Shipping route — broad, not just rivers or coastal roads.

en.question: How must traffic separation schemes be navigated?
answers: They may only be navigated in the general direction of traffic flow to the right of the separation line or separation zone.
They may only be navigated in the direction of travel to the left of the separation line or separation zone.
Within the outer separation lines, they may only be navigated in one direction of travel.
They may only be navigated from start to finish and only to the right of the separation zone in the direction of travel.

explanation.de: Regel 10 der KVR schreibt vor, dass Fahrzeuge in einem Verkehrstrennungsgebiet die jeweils vorgesehene Fahrspur in der allgemeinen Verkehrsrichtung benutzen und dabei rechts der Trennlinie oder Trennzone bleiben müssen. Antwort (b) ist falsch, weil sie 'links' angibt; Antwort (c) ist zu ungenau, da innerhalb der äußeren Grenzen beide Spuren (je eine Richtung) verlaufen.
explanation.en: COLREG Rule 10 requires vessels using a traffic separation scheme to proceed in the appropriate traffic lane in the general direction of traffic flow for that lane, keeping to the right of the separation line or zone. Answer (b) is wrong because it states 'left', and (c) is too vague — both lanes exist within the outer boundaries, each for one direction.
explanation.memoryAid: Keep RIGHT of the dividing line — just like driving on the road.

en.question: What does 'in sight of one another' mean?
answers: When each vessel can be visually observed by the other.
When each vessel's operator can be visually observed by the other.
When both vessels can be visually observed.
When each vessel can be visually observed even in restricted visibility.

explanation.de: "In Sicht befindlich" bedeutet nach den KVR (COLREG Regel 3m), dass jedes Fahrzeug das andere optisch wahrnehmen kann. Entscheidend ist die gegenseitige optische Wahrnehmbarkeit der Fahrzeuge selbst – nicht ihrer Führenden (Antwort b) und nicht in unsichtigem Wetter (Antwort d), da bei eingeschränkter Sicht gerade die besonderen Regeln für unsichtiges Wetter gelten.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 3(k), vessels are 'in sight of one another' only when one can be observed visually from the other. The key is mutual visual observation of the vessels themselves — not their operators (option b), and specifically not in restricted visibility (option d), as restricted visibility triggers a separate set of rules.
explanation.memoryAid: Vessels in sight = eyes on the hull, not on the skipper.

en.question: What does 'safe speed' mean?
answers: The speed must be adapted to the traffic situation, visibility, and weather conditions, and it must be possible to stop the vessel at any time.
The speed must be adapted to the traffic situation, visibility, and weather conditions, and traffic must not be impeded.
The speed must be adapted to the traffic situation, visibility, weather conditions, and fuel consumption.
The speed must be adapted to the traffic situation, traffic volume, sea state, and wind conditions so that no suction or wash is created.

explanation.de: Sichere Geschwindigkeit gemäß COLREG Regel 6 bedeutet, dass ein Fahrzeug so langsam fahren muss, dass es jederzeit anhalten kann, um eine Kollision zu vermeiden. Die Anpassung an Verkehrslage, Sicht und Wetter ist notwendige Bedingung, aber entscheidend ist die Möglichkeit, jederzeit aufzustoppen. Antwort b ist falsch, weil 'den Verkehr nicht behindern' eine andere Regelung ist; c und d enthalten sachfremde Zusätze wie Treibstoffverbrauch oder Wellenschlag, die nicht zum Kerninhalt der sicheren Geschwindigkeit gehören.
explanation.en: Safe speed under COLREG Rule 6 means a vessel must proceed at a speed that allows it to take proper and effective action to avoid collision and stop within an appropriate distance. Adapting to traffic, visibility, and weather is required, but the defining element is the ability to stop at any time. Answer b is incorrect because 'not impeding traffic' is a separate rule; c and d introduce irrelevant criteria such as fuel consumption or wash that are not part of the safe speed concept.
explanation.memoryAid: Safe speed = Safe STOP: you must always be able to stop in time.

en.question: Which vessel displays these lights?
answers: A power-driven vessel underway of less than 50 m in length.
A power-driven vessel underway of 50 m or more in length.
A vessel not under command underway.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way through the water, of 50 m or more in length.

explanation.de: Ein Maschinenfahrzeug unter 50 m Länge in Fahrt darf das Topplicht und Hecklicht zu einem weißen Rundumlicht zusammenfassen (oder zeigt nur ein Topplicht vorne), dazu Seitenlichter und Hecklicht. Fahrzeuge ab 50 m Länge müssen zwei getrennte Topplichter (vorne und hinten) führen. Manövrierunfähige oder manöverbehinderte Fahrzeuge zeigen zusätzliche charakteristische Lichter (z. B. Rot-Weiß-Rot oder Rot-Weiß Rundumlichter), die hier nicht vorhanden sind.
explanation.en: A power-driven vessel under 50 m in length underway may combine the masthead light and sternlight into a single all-round white light (or show one masthead light forward), sidelights, and a sternlight. Vessels of 50 m or more must carry two separate masthead lights (fore and aft). Vessels not under command and those restricted in their ability to manoeuvre show additional distinctive lights (e.g. red-white-red or red-white lights all-round), which are not present here.
explanation.memoryAid: Under 50 m = one masthead light is enough; 50 m or more = two masthead lights required.

en.question: Which vessel must display these lights?
answers: Power-driven vessel underway, 50 metres or more in length.
Power-driven vessel underway, less than 50 metres in length.
A vessel not under command, underway.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way through the water, 50 metres or more in length.

explanation.de: Ein Maschinenfahrzeug von 50 Metern Länge oder mehr muss in Fahrt ein vorderes Topplicht, ein zweites (hinteres) Topplicht, Seitenlichter und ein Hecklicht führen. Die Pflicht zum zweiten Topplicht gilt gemäß Regel 23 KVR erst ab 50 m Länge, weshalb Antwort (b) falsch ist. Manövrierunfähige oder manövriergehinderte Fahrzeuge zeigen andere Lichter gemäß Regel 27 KVR, daher sind (c) und (d) ebenfalls falsch.
explanation.en: A power-driven vessel of 50 metres or more in length underway must display a foremast masthead light, a second (aft) masthead light higher and further aft than the forward one, sidelights, and a sternlight. The requirement for a second masthead light applies specifically to vessels 50 m or longer (COLREG Rule 23). Vessels under 50 m may carry a second masthead light but are not required to, so answer (b) is incorrect. A vessel not under command or restricted in manoeuvrability would show different all-round light configurations (Rules 27), making (c) and (d) wrong.
explanation.memoryAid: Two masthead lights stacked = 50+ metres stacked.

en.question: Which vessel displays these lights?
answers: A restricted in ability to manoeuvre towing vessel underway, with a tow length of 200 metres or less.
A restricted in ability to manoeuvre towing vessel underway, with a tow length of more than 200 metres.
A restricted in ability to manoeuvre towing vessel underway, with a tow length of 200 metres or less, but without way through the water.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way through the water, of 50 metres or more in length.

explanation.de: Ein in seiner Manövrierfähigkeit behindertes Fahrzeug, das schleppt, führt die RAM-Lichter (rot-weiß-rot übereinander) sowie die Schlepplichter (zwei Topplichter, Seiten- und Hecklicht mit gelbem Schlepplicht). Zwei Topplichter statt drei zeigen an, dass die Schlepplänge 200 m oder weniger beträgt. Da das Fahrzeug Fahrt durchs Wasser macht, entfällt Option c; da es ein Schleppverband ist, entfällt Option d.
explanation.en: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre that is towing shows the RAM lights (two red-white-red all-round lights in a vertical line) plus the towing masthead lights and sternlight. When the tow is 200 metres or less, only two masthead lights are shown; a tow exceeding 200 metres would require three masthead lights. The vessel here shows two masthead lights with sidelights and a towing light, indicating the 200 m or less configuration with way on, which rules out option c (no way) and option d (no tow).
explanation.memoryAid: 2 mastheads = tow ≤ 200 m; 3 mastheads = tow > 200 m.

en.question: Which vessel is showing these lights?
answers: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre: a towing vessel with a tow exceeding 200 metres in length, underway and making way.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre: a towing vessel with a tow of 200 metres or less in length, underway and making way.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre: a towing vessel with a tow exceeding 200 metres in length, underway but not making way through the water.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, engaged in dredging or underwater operations, and impeding navigation.

explanation.de: Ein manövrierbehinderter Schleppverband mit einer Schleppzuglänge von mehr als 200 m zeigt zusätzlich zum normalen Schlepplicht (Masttopplicht, zwei Topplichte übereinander, Seitenlichter, Hecklicht) einen dritten Masttopp sowie das Drei-Lichter-Zeichen (Rot-Weiß-Rot) für Manövrierbehinderung. Liegt die Schlepplänge bei 200 m oder weniger, entfällt das dritte Topplicht (Antwort b wäre falsch). Ohne Fahrt durchs Wasser würden Seiten- und Hecklicht erlöschen (Antwort c wäre falsch).
explanation.en: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre towing a vessel where the length of tow exceeds 200 metres shows three masthead lights in a vertical line (instead of two), plus the red-white-red all-round lights indicating restricted manoeuvrability, sidelights and sternlight. Answer b is wrong because a tow of 200 m or less requires only two masthead lights. Answer c is wrong because a vessel not making way through the water would not show sidelights or a sternlight.
explanation.memoryAid: Three mastheads = tow over 200 m; two mastheads = tow 200 m or under.

en.question: What lights must a vessel being towed display?
answers: Sidelights red and green, and one white sternlight.
Sidelights red and green, and one white all-round light.
Sidelights red and green, and two red all-round lights in a vertical line.
Sidelights red and green, and a red all-round light vertically above a white all-round light.

explanation.de: Gemäß KVR Regel 24(e) führt ein geschlepptes Fahrzeug Seitenlichter (rot und grün) sowie ein weißes Hecklicht – also dieselben Lichter wie ein gewöhnliches Fahrzeug unter Fahrt, jedoch ohne Topplicht. Die Antworten mit Rundumlichtern sind falsch, da diese anderen Fahrzeugkategorien (z. B. manövrierunfähige oder manövrierbehinderte Fahrzeuge) vorbehalten sind.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 24(e), a vessel being towed displays sidelights (red to port, green to starboard) and a white sternlight — the same lights as an ordinary underway vessel, but without a masthead light. The distractors incorrectly substitute all-round lights for the sternlight, which would instead indicate special vessel status (e.g. restricted ability to manoeuvre or not under command).
explanation.memoryAid: Towed = normal underway lights minus the masthead: sides + stern only.

en.question: What does it mean when every vessel in a tow displays a black diamond shape?
answers: Tow exceeding 200 metres in length.
Tow exceeding 100 metres in length.
Tow exceeding 50 metres in length.
Tow less than 50 metres in length.

explanation.de: Gemäß COLREG Regel 24 führt jedes Fahrzeug eines Schleppverbandes einen schwarzen Rhombus, wenn die Gesamtlänge des Schleppverbandes mehr als 200 m beträgt. Die anderen Antworten geben falsche Grenzwerte an.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 24, every vessel in a tow must display a black diamond shape when the length of the tow exceeds 200 metres. The other answer options state incorrect threshold lengths.
explanation.memoryAid: Diamond = Double century: the diamond shape appears when the tow tops 200 m.

en.question: Which vessel displays these lights?
answers: A vessel not under command, underway.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, underway.
A vessel constrained by her draught, underway.
A vessel aground of 50 metres or more in length.

explanation.de: Ein manövrierunfähiges Fahrzeug in Fahrt zeigt zwei rote Rundumlichter übereinander (ohne Dampferlichter). Ein manövrierbehindertes Fahrzeug würde zusätzlich Rot-Weiß-Rot zeigen, und ein tiefgangbehindertes Fahrzeug zeigt drei rote Rundumlichter übereinander.
explanation.en: A vessel not under command (NUC) underway shows two all-round red lights in a vertical line, with no masthead or sidelights when making no way (or adding sidelights/sternlight when making way). A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre would show red-white-red all-round lights, and a vessel constrained by draught shows three all-round red lights — making those distractors incorrect.
explanation.memoryAid: NUC = two reds stacked — 'Not Under Control, seeing red twice.'

en.question: Which vessel displays these lights?
answers: A vessel not under command, making way through the water.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way through the water, of 50 metres or more in length.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way through the water.
A fishing vessel (trawler), making way through the water, of 50 metres or more in length.

explanation.de: Ein manövrierunfähiges Fahrzeug führt zwei rote Rundumlichter übereinander; macht es Fahrt durchs Wasser, kommen Seitenlichter und Hecklicht hinzu. Ein manövrierbehindertes Fahrzeug würde dagegen rot-weiß-rot (drei Lichter) zeigen, ein Trawler grün-weiß.
explanation.en: A vessel not under command displays two all-round red lights in a vertical line; when making way through the water, sidelights and a sternlight are added. A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre would show red-white-red (three lights), and a trawler would show green-white all-round lights.
explanation.memoryAid: Not under command = 2 Reds (NUC = No Unplanned Colours beyond red).

en.question: Which vessel displays these shapes?
answers: A vessel not under command.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, underway.
A vessel engaged in fishing, underway.
A vessel aground of 50 metres or more in length.

explanation.de: Zwei schwarze Bälle übereinander sind das Tagessignal eines manövrierunfähigen Fahrzeugs. Ein manövrierbehindertes Fahrzeug führt Ball-Raute-Ball, und ein Grundsitzer führt drei Bälle übereinander.
explanation.en: Two black balls displayed in a vertical line indicate a vessel not under command (NUC). A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre would display a ball-diamond-ball combination, and a vessel aground would show three balls in a vertical line.
explanation.memoryAid: Two balls = 'can't move at all' (not under command).

en.question: What lights must a vessel of 12 metres or more in length, not under command, show when underway but making no way through the water?
answers: Two all-round red lights in a vertical line.
Two all-round red lights in a vertical line, plus sidelights and a sternlight.
Three all-round red lights in a vertical line.
Three all-round red lights in a vertical line, plus sidelights and a sternlight.

explanation.de: Ein manövrierunfähiges Fahrzeug (≥ 12 m) zeigt zwei rote Rundumlichter senkrecht übereinander (COLREG Regel 27a). Nur wenn das Fahrzeug tatsächlich Fahrt durch das Wasser macht, kommen Seiten- und Hecklicht hinzu; ohne Fahrt durch das Wasser entfallen diese. Drei rote Rundumlichter gelten für tiefgangbeschränkte Fahrzeuge, nicht für manövrierunfähige.
explanation.en: A vessel not under command (≥ 12 m) displays two all-round red lights in a vertical line (COLREG Rule 27a). Sidelights and a sternlight are only added when the vessel is actually making way through the water; with no way on, they are omitted. Three all-round red lights apply to vessels constrained by their draught, not to vessels not under command.
explanation.memoryAid: NUC = 2 red balls by day, 2 red lights by night — add side/stern lights only when making way.

en.question: What lights must a vessel of 12 metres or more in length that is not under command display when underway and making way through the water?
answers: Two all-round red lights in a vertical line and, in addition, the sidelights and the sternlight.
Two all-round red lights in a vertical line.
Three all-round red lights in a vertical line.
Three all-round red lights in a vertical line and, in addition, the sidelights and the sternlight.

explanation.de: Ein manövrierunfähiges Fahrzeug (≥ 12 m) zeigt gemäß COLREG Regel 27 zwei rote Rundumlichter senkrecht übereinander. Wenn es Fahrt durch das Wasser macht, kommen zusätzlich Seitenlichter und Hecklicht hinzu. Ohne Fahrt durchs Wasser entfallen Seiten- und Hecklicht. Drei rote Rundumlichter sind das Signal für ein tiefgangbehindertes Fahrzeug (Regel 28), nicht für ein manövrierunfähiges.
explanation.en: A vessel not under command (≥ 12 m) displays two all-round red lights in a vertical line per COLREG Rule 27. When making way through the water, sidelights and a sternlight are added. Without way through the water, sidelights and sternlight are omitted. Three all-round red lights in a vertical line indicate a vessel constrained by her draught (Rule 28), not one that is not under command.
explanation.memoryAid: 2 red = Not Under Command; add sidelights + sternlight only when actually MOVING through the water.

en.question: Which vessel displays these lights?
answers: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, underway.
A vessel not under command, underway.
A fishing vessel underway.
A vessel aground of less than 50 m in length.

explanation.de: Ein manövrierbehindertes Fahrzeug in Fahrt führt neben den normalen Fahrlichtern (Seitenlichter und Hecklicht) drei zusätzliche Rundumlichter senkrecht übereinander: rot-weiß-rot. Ein manövrierunfähiges Fahrzeug zeigt hingegen nur zwei rote Rundumlichter (ohne das weiße Licht in der Mitte), und ein Grundsitzer zeigt drei Rundumlichter rot-weiß-rot nur vor Anker, nicht in Fahrt.
explanation.en: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre (RAM) displays, in addition to normal underway lights (sidelights and sternlight), three all-round lights in a vertical line: red–white–red. A vessel not under command shows only two red all-round lights (no white light in the middle), so that option is incorrect. A vessel aground shows red–white–red all-round lights only at anchor, not underway.
explanation.memoryAid: RAM = Red-White-Red (sandwich): the white in the middle marks 'Restricted' not 'Not under command'.

en.question: Which vessel must carry these lights?
answers: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, underway and making way, of 50 metres or more in length.
A vessel not under command, underway and making way, of 50 metres or more in length.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, underway but not making way, of 50 metres or more in length.
A fishing vessel trawling, underway and making way, of 50 metres or more in length.

explanation.de: Ein manövrierbehindertes Fahrzeug (RAM), das Fahrt durchs Wasser macht, führt zusätzlich zu den RAM-Lichtern (rot-weiß-rot Rundumlichter) Seitenlichter, Hecklicht und – ab 50 m Länge – ein zweites Topplicht. Ein manövrierunfähiges Fahrzeug (NUC) zeigt dagegen nur zwei rote Rundumlichter und keine Topplichter. Ein Trawler verwendet eine andere Lichtkombination. Ein RAM-Fahrzeug ohne Fahrt durchs Wasser würde keine Seitenlichter oder Topplichter führen.
explanation.en: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre (RAM) that is making way through the water shows, in addition to the RAM lights (two red-white-red all-round lights), her sidelights, sternlight, and – at 50 m or more – a second masthead light. A vessel not under command (NUC) shows only two red all-round lights plus sidelights/sternlight when making way, without masthead lights. A trawler uses a different combination (green-over-white all-round lights). A RAM vessel stopped in the water (not making way) would not show sidelights or masthead lights.
explanation.memoryAid: RAM + way = full steaming lights added on top of the red-white-red stack.

en.question: Which vessel carries these shapes?
answers: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.
A vessel not under command, underway.
A fishing vessel underway.
A vessel aground of less than 50 m in length.

explanation.de: Ein manövrierbehindertes Fahrzeug führt als Tagzeichen zwei Bälle und eine Raute (Ball–Raute–Ball) in senkrechter Linie. Dieses Zeichen unterscheidet es von einem manövrierunfähigen Fahrzeug (zwei Bälle übereinander) und einem Grundsitzer (drei Bälle übereinander).
explanation.en: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre displays, as day shapes, a ball–diamond–ball arrangement in a vertical line. This distinguishes it from a vessel not under command (two balls in a vertical line) and a vessel aground (three balls in a vertical line).
explanation.memoryAid: Ball-Diamond-Ball = 'Restricted' — the diamond in the middle marks the restriction.

en.question: Which vessel displays these lights?
answers: A vessel aground less than 50 m in length.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.
A vessel not under command, underway.
A vessel aground 50 m or more in length.

explanation.de: Ein Grundsitzer (auf Grund liegend) von weniger als 50 m Länge führt zwei rote Rundumlichter übereinander sowie die vorgeschriebenen Ankerlichter (ein weißes Rundumlicht). Fahrzeuge von 50 m und mehr müssen zusätzlich ein weiteres Ankerlicht zeigen. Ein manövrierbehindertes oder manövrierunfähiges Fahrzeug zeigt eine andere Lichtkombination (rot-weiß-rot bzw. rot-rot).
explanation.en: A vessel aground less than 50 m in length displays two all-round red lights in a vertical line plus the anchor light(s) (one all-round white light). Vessels of 50 m or more must show an additional anchor light. A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre or not under command shows a different combination of lights (red-white-red or red-red respectively).
explanation.memoryAid: Aground = Anchor light(s) + two Reds on top — under 50 m needs only one white anchor light.

en.question: Which vessel displays these shapes?
answers: A vessel aground.
A vessel not under command.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.
A vessel engaged in fishing.

explanation.de: Ein Grundsitzer führt bei Tag drei Bälle senkrecht übereinander. Dieses Signal unterscheidet ihn von einem manövrierunfähigen Fahrzeug (zwei Bälle) oder einem manövrierbehinderten Fahrzeug (Kugel-Rhombus-Kugel).
explanation.en: A vessel aground displays three black balls in a vertical line as her day signal. This distinguishes her from a vessel not under command (two balls) or a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre (ball–diamond–ball).
explanation.memoryAid: Three balls = stuck on the bottom — one ball for each point of contact: bow, middle, stern.

en.question: Which vessel displays these lights?
answers: A vessel aground, 50 metres or more in length.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.
A vessel not under command, underway.
A vessel aground, less than 50 metres in length.

explanation.de: Ein Grundsitzer von 50 m Länge oder mehr führt gemäß KVR (COLREG) die Lichter für ein auf Grund geratenes Fahrzeug (zwei Rundumlichter übereinander, rot-rot) sowie zusätzlich die Ankerlichter (vorne ein weißes Rundumlicht, achtern ein weiteres). Fahrzeuge unter 50 m Länge auf Grund benötigen das achterliche Ankerlicht nicht. Ein manövrierbehindertes oder manövrierunfähiges Fahrzeug führt andere Lichtkombinationen.
explanation.en: A vessel aground of 50 metres or more in length displays the aground lights (two all-round red lights in a vertical line) plus both an forward and an after all-round white anchor light. Vessels aground under 50 m in length are not required to show the after anchor light. Vessels restricted in ability to manoeuvre or not under command show different light configurations.
explanation.memoryAid: Big grounded ships (50 m+) need BOTH anchor lights — fore and aft — plus the two red all-round lights.

en.question: Which vessel must display these lights?
answers: A vessel constrained by her draught, 50 metres or more in length, underway.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.
A vessel not under command.
A vessel aground, less than 50 metres in length.

explanation.de: Ein tiefgangbehindertes Fahrzeug (ab 50 m Länge, in Fahrt) führt die normalen Topplichter, Seitenlichter und das Hecklicht eines Maschinenfahrzeugs sowie zusätzlich drei rote Rundumlichte übereinander. Manövrierbehindertes Fahrzeug zeigt rot-weiß-rot, manövrierunfähiges Fahrzeug zeigt zwei rote Rundumlichte, und ein Grundsitzer zeigt Ankerlichter plus zwei rote Rundumlichte.
explanation.en: A vessel constrained by her draught (50 m or more, underway) shows the normal masthead lights, sidelights, and sternlight of a power-driven vessel PLUS three all-round red lights in a vertical line. This distinguishes her from a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre (which shows red-white-red all-round lights) and a vessel not under command (which shows two red all-round lights). A vessel aground displays anchor lights plus two red all-round lights, not this combination.
explanation.memoryAid: Constrained by Draught = normal steaming lights + three reds stacked — the deepest vessel gets the most red lights.

en.question: Which vessel displays these shapes?
answers: A vessel constrained by her draught, underway.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, underway.
A vessel not under command, underway.
A vessel aground of less than 50 metres in length.

explanation.de: Ein tiefgangbehindertes Fahrzeug führt als Tagessignal einen Zylinder (drei schwarze Bälle übereinander sind für manövrierunfähige Fahrzeuge; der Zylinder ist das spezifische Zeichen für tiefgangbehinderte Fahrzeuge gemäß KVR). Manövrierunfähige Fahrzeuge zeigen zwei schwarze Bälle, Grundsitzer zeigen drei Bälle.
explanation.en: A vessel constrained by her draught displays a cylinder as her day shape. This is a specific COLREG shape unique to draught-constrained vessels. By contrast, a vessel not under command displays two black balls, and a vessel aground displays three black balls — making those distractors incorrect.
explanation.memoryAid: CYlinder = Constrained by draught — the shape is as 'deep' as the vessel's problem.

en.question: Which vessel must display these lights?
answers: A trawler (fishing vessel) making way through the water, of 50 metres or more in length.
A fishing vessel underway that is not trawling, e.g. a drift-net fisher.
A government/authority vessel on duty.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, underway.

explanation.de: Gemäß Regel 26 der KVR muss ein trawlendes Fischereifahrzeug ab 50 Meter Länge neben den zwei Fischereilichtern (grün über weiß), Seitenlichtern und Hecklicht zusätzlich ein zweites (höheres, achterliches) Topplicht führen — genau dieses zweite Topplicht unterscheidet einen Trawler ≥50 m von einem kleineren. Nicht trawlende Fischereifahrzeuge zeigen rot über weiß, und manövrierbe­hinderte Fahrzeuge führen drei Rundumlichter (rot-weiß-rot).
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 26, a vessel engaged in trawling that is 50 metres or more in length must display the two trawling lights (green over white), sidelights, a sternlight, AND a second (higher, after) masthead light — that additional masthead light is what distinguishes a trawler of ≥50 m from a smaller trawler. Drift-net fishers and non-trawling fishing vessels show a different light combination (red over white), so answer B is wrong. Vessels restricted in their ability to manoeuvre show three all-round lights (red-white-red), not this combination.
explanation.memoryAid: Trawler at 50+: Green-White fishing lights PLUS a second masthead light — the bigger the trawler, the more lights on top.

en.question: Which vessel displays these lights?
answers: A fishing vessel underway or at anchor, not trawling, e.g. a drift-net fisher.
A pilot vessel on duty.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, underway.
A trawler (fishing vessel) making way through the water, 50 metres or more in length.

explanation.de: Gemäß Regel 26 KVR zeigt ein fischendes Fahrzeug, das nicht trawlt (z. B. Treibnetzfischer), zwei Rundumlichter übereinander – Rot über Weiß – sowie bei Fahrt durch das Wasser Seiten- und Hecklicht. Ein Trawler zeigt dagegen Grün über Weiß, ein Lotsenfahrzeug Weiß über Rot, und ein manövrierbehindertes Fahrzeug Rot-Weiß-Rot.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 26, a fishing vessel not trawling (e.g. using nets, lines, or drift nets) shows two all-round lights in a vertical line — red over white — plus sidelights and a sternlight when making way. A trawler instead shows green over white. A pilot vessel shows white over red, and a vessel restricted in ability to manoeuvre shows red-white-red.
explanation.memoryAid: Not trawling = Red over White (R-W like 'Right answer').

en.question: Which vessel displays these shapes?
answers: A vessel engaged in fishing, whether underway or at anchor.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.
A vessel not under command, underway.
A vessel aground of less than 50 m in length.

explanation.de: Zwei Kegel mit den Spitzen zusammen (Doppelkegel) sind das Tageszeichen für fischende Fahrzeuge (außer Trawler) gemäß Regel 26 der KVR, unabhängig davon, ob sie fahren oder vor Anker liegen. Ein manövrierunfähiges Fahrzeug führt zwei schwarze Bälle; ein Grundsitzer führt drei schwarze Bälle.
explanation.en: Two cones with their apexes together (a double cone or 'diamond' shape) is the dayshape prescribed for vessels engaged in fishing (other than trawling) under COLREG Rule 26. This applies whether the vessel is underway or at anchor. A vessel not under command displays two black balls; a vessel aground displays three black balls.
explanation.memoryAid: Two cones tip-to-tip = fishing ship — the shape looks like a fish caught between two nets.

en.question: Which vessels show only sidelights (red and green) and a white sternlight?
answers: Sailing vessels, rowing boats, and vessels being towed.
Sailing vessels, rowing boats, and power-driven vessels underway of less than 50 m in length.
Sailing vessels, fishing vessels, and vessels being towed.
Sailing vessels, vessels aground, and vessels being towed.

explanation.de: Segelfahrzeuge (unter Segel), Ruderboote und geschleppte Fahrzeuge führen als einzige Fahrzeuggruppen ausschließlich Seitenlichter (rot/grün) und ein weißes Hecklicht – ohne Topplicht. Maschinenfahrzeuge benötigen zusätzlich mindestens ein weißes Topplicht, fischende Fahrzeuge haben spezielle Zusatzlichter, und Grundsitzer führen andere Signallichter.
explanation.en: Sailing vessels (under sail), rowing boats, and vessels being towed are the only categories that show exclusively sidelights (red/green) and a white sternlight — without a masthead (steaming) light. Power-driven vessels require at least one white masthead light in addition, fishing vessels carry special additional lights, and vessels aground display different signals.
explanation.memoryAid: No engine, no masthead: sailors, rowers, and towed vessels all share the same minimal light set.

en.question: What light must a vessel at anchor of less than 50 metres in length exhibit?
answers: One all-round white light in a prominent position.
One all-round red light in a prominent position.
Two all-round white lights in a prominent position.
Two all-round red lights in a prominent position.

explanation.de: Gemäß KVR Regel 30 muss ein Fahrzeug unter 50 m Länge beim Ankern ein einzelnes weißes Rundumlicht an gut sichtbarer Stelle führen. Zwei weiße Rundumlichter (vorne oben, hinten niedriger) sind erst für Fahrzeuge ab 50 m Länge vorgeschrieben. Rote Rundumlichter gelten für andere Situationen, z. B. für manövrierunfähige Fahrzeuge.
explanation.en: According to COLREG Rule 30, a vessel under 50 metres in length at anchor must exhibit a single all-round white light in a prominent position. Two all-round white lights (one forward at the bow, one lower at the stern) are only required for vessels of 50 metres or more. Red all-round lights apply to other situations, such as vessels not under command.
explanation.memoryAid: Small anchor = one white globe: under 50 m, one light is enough.

en.question: Which vessel must display these lights?
answers: A vessel at anchor of 100 metres or more in length.
A fishing trawler (fishing vessel) underway through the water of 50 metres or more in length.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, engaged in dredging or underwater operations, and impeding navigation.
A vessel aground of 200 metres or more in length.

explanation.de: Ein vor Anker liegendes Fahrzeug ab 100 m Länge muss nach KVR Regel 30 zusätzlich zum normalen Ankerlicht (weißes Rundumlicht vorne und achtern) auch alle verfügbaren Arbeitslichter einschalten, um die Form und Ausdehnung des Fahrzeugs zu beleuchten. Das unterscheidet es von kürzeren Ankerliegern.
explanation.en: A vessel at anchor of 100 metres or more in length must, under COLREG Rule 30, illuminate its decks in addition to the standard anchor lights (forward and aft all-round white lights). This additional deck lighting distinguishes large anchored vessels from shorter ones and from the other vessel types listed as distractors.

en.question: In restricted visibility, you hear at least every two minutes one prolonged blast on the whistle ( ). Which vessel gives this signal?
answers: A power-driven vessel making way through the water.
A vessel being towed, or the last manned vessel of a tow underway.
A vessel carrying dangerous cargo, at anchor, of less than 100 m in length.
A vessel at anchor of 100 metres or more in length.

explanation.de: Nach KVR Regel 35(a) gibt ein Maschinenfahrzeug, das Fahrt durchs Wasser macht, bei verminderter Sicht mindestens alle zwei Minuten einen langen Ton. Ein geschlepptes Fahrzeug gibt hingegen einen langen und drei kurze Töne (–•••). Fahrzeuge vor Anker geben ein Glockensignal, kein Pfeifensignal.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 35(a), a power-driven vessel making way through the water sounds one prolonged blast at intervals of not more than two minutes in restricted visibility. A vessel being towed sounds one prolonged blast followed by three short blasts (–•••). Vessels at anchor ring a bell, not a whistle blast.
explanation.memoryAid: One long blast = lone power vessel ploughing ahead through the fog.

en.question: In restricted visibility, you hear at least every two minutes two successive prolonged blasts on the whistle ( ). Which vessel gives this signal?
answers: A power-driven vessel underway that has stopped her engines and is making no way through the water.
A vessel being towed, or the last manned vessel of a tow underway.
A vessel with dangerous cargo at anchor, less than 100 metres in length.
A vessel at anchor, 100 metres or more in length.

explanation.de: Zwei aufeinanderfolgende lange Töne (mit einer Pause von etwa zwei Sekunden dazwischen) signalisieren gemäß den Kollisionsverhütungsregeln (KVR/COLREG Regel 35) ein Maschinenfahrzeug in Fahrt, das seine Maschine gestoppt hat und keine Fahrt durchs Wasser macht. Ein fahrendes Maschinenfahrzeug mit Fahrt würde nur einen langen Ton geben; ankernde Fahrzeuge verwenden Glockensignale.
explanation.en: Two successive prolonged blasts (with an interval of about two seconds between them) indicate, under COLREG Rule 35, a power-driven vessel underway that has stopped her engines and is making no way through the water. A power-driven vessel making way gives one prolonged blast; vessels at anchor use bell signals instead.
explanation.memoryAid: Two blasts = 'stopped' — engines stopped, no way, two notes to say 'I'm going nowhere'.

en.question: Which vessels, in restricted visibility, sound at least every two minutes three successive blasts on the whistle — one prolonged followed by two short blasts?
answers: A vessel not under command underway, a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre underway or at anchor, a vessel constrained by her draught underway, a sailing vessel underway, a vessel engaged in towing or pushing underway, a vessel engaged in fishing underway or at anchor.

A vessel not under command underway, a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre underway or at anchor, a vessel constrained by her draught underway, a power-driven vessel underway making way through the water, a vessel engaged in towing or pushing underway, a vessel engaged in fishing underway or at anchor.

A vessel not under command underway, a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre underway or at anchor, a vessel constrained by her draught underway, a sailing vessel underway, a vessel engaged in towing or pushing underway, a vessel engaged in fishing underway or at anchor, a power-driven vessel underway that has stopped her engines and is making no way through the water.

A vessel not under command underway, a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre underway or at anchor, a vessel constrained by her draught underway, a sailing vessel underway, a vessel engaged in towing or pushing underway, a vessel being towed or the last manned vessel of a tow underway, a vessel engaged in fishing underway or at anchor.

explanation.de: Nach COLREG Regel 35 geben manövrierunfähige, manöverbehinderte, tiefgangbehinderte, segelnde, schleppende/schiebende und fischende Fahrzeuge in Fahrt (sowie manöverbehinderte und fischende Fahrzeuge vor Anker) das Nebelzeichen lang-kurz-kurz. Antwort b ist falsch, weil Maschinenfahrzeuge mit Fahrt das Zeichen lang-lang (alle zwei Minuten einen langen Ton) geben. Antwort d ist falsch, weil geschleppte Fahrzeuge ebenfalls lang-kurz-kurz geben dürfen, aber sie sind keine Pflichtbestandteile der Grundgruppe dieser Frage – sie können das Signal geben, sind aber nicht in der Kernliste der primär verpflichteten Fahrzeuge.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 35, vessels not under command, restricted in ability to manoeuvre, constrained by draught, sailing vessels, vessels towing/pushing, and fishing vessels underway (plus vessels restricted in ability to manoeuvre and fishing vessels at anchor) sound one prolonged and two short blasts in restricted visibility. Answer b is wrong because a power-driven vessel making way sounds one prolonged blast every two minutes, not this signal. Answer d incorrectly includes towed vessels, which may optionally sound this signal but are not part of the primary obligated group listed in Rule 35.
explanation.memoryAid: Think '1 long + 2 short = Special vessels' — everyone who is NOT a normal power-driven vessel making way uses this signal.

en.question: Which vessel, in restricted visibility, gives four successive blasts on the whistle — long, short, short, short — immediately following the signal long, short, short?
answers: A vessel being towed, or the last manned vessel in a tow, underway.
A power-driven vessel underway that has stopped her engines and is making no way through the water.
A vessel with dangerous cargo at anchor, less than 100 metres in length.
A vessel not under command, less than 100 metres in length.

explanation.de: Ein geschlepptes Fahrzeug (oder das letzte bemannte Fahrzeug eines Schleppverbandes) gibt in Fahrt bei verminderter Sicht nach dem Signal des schleppenden Fahrzeugs (lang, kurz, kurz) unmittelbar danach vier Töne: lang, kurz, kurz, kurz. Das zusätzliche kurze Signal kennzeichnet das geschleppte Fahrzeug und unterscheidet es vom schleppenden Fahrzeug (lang, kurz, kurz).
explanation.en: A vessel being towed (or the last manned vessel in a tow) underway in restricted visibility sounds, immediately after the towing vessel's signal (long, short, short), four blasts: long, short, short, short. The extra short blast identifies the towed vessel and distinguishes it from the towing vessel's signal of long, short, short.
explanation.memoryAid: Towing vessel: L-S-S; Towed vessel adds one more short: L-S-S-S.

en.question: What sound signal must a sailing vessel underway of 12 metres or more in length give in restricted visibility?
answers: At least every two minutes, three successive blasts on the whistle: one prolonged followed by two short blasts
At least every two minutes, three successive blasts on the whistle: two prolonged followed by one short blast
At least every two minutes, one powerful sound signal that cannot be confused with the prescribed signals
On the whistle: short, prolonged, short

explanation.de: Gemäß KVR (COLREG) Regel 35 muss ein Segelfahrzeug in Fahrt bei verminderter Sicht mindestens alle zwei Minuten drei aufeinanderfolgende Töne geben: einen langen und zwei kurze Töne (▬ • •). Dieses Signal unterscheidet sich bewusst vom Signal eines Maschinenfahrzeugs in Fahrt (ein langer Ton) und ist spezifisch für Segelfahrzeuge sowie manövrierbehinderte oder festgemachte Fahrzeuge nach Regel 35.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 35, a sailing vessel underway in restricted visibility must sound at least every two minutes three successive blasts: one prolonged followed by two short blasts (▬ • •). This distinguishes it from a power-driven vessel underway (one prolonged blast) and is the prescribed signal specifically for sailing vessels and certain other vessel categories.
explanation.memoryAid: Sailing = '1 long, 2 short' — think of a sailboat's triangular sail shape: one tall mast, two short booms (▬ • •).

en.question: What sound signal must a vessel underway of less than 12 metres in length make in restricted visibility if it is unable to give the otherwise prescribed sound signals?
answers: At least every two minutes, one efficient sound signal that cannot be mistaken for any of the prescribed signals.
At least every two minutes, three successive blasts on the whistle: one prolonged, two short.
At least every two minutes, three successive blasts on the whistle: two prolonged, one short.
One short, one prolonged, one short blast on the whistle.

explanation.de: Nach COLREG Regel 35 müssen Fahrzeuge bei verminderter Sicht bestimmte Schallsignale geben. Für Fahrzeuge unter 12 m Länge, die diese vorgeschriebenen Signale nicht erzeugen können, gilt eine Ausnahme: Sie müssen mindestens alle zwei Minuten irgendein kräftiges Schallsignal geben, solange es nicht mit den regulären Signalen verwechselt werden kann. Die Antworten b und c beschreiben Nebelsignale für andere Fahrzeugtypen (z. B. manövrierunfähige oder eingeschränkt manövrierfähige Fahrzeuge), nicht diese Ausnahmeregelung.
explanation.en: COLREG Rule 35 prescribes fog signals for vessels in restricted visibility. For vessels under 12 m in length that cannot produce the normally required signals, an exemption applies: they must make at least one efficient sound signal every two minutes, provided it cannot be confused with the prescribed signals. Options b and c describe fog signals used by other specific vessel categories, not this exemption for small craft.
explanation.memoryAid: Small boat, no proper gear? Just make ANY loud noise every 2 minutes — as long as it sounds different from the official signals.

en.question: Which vessel sounds rapid ringing of the bell for approximately 5 seconds at intervals of not more than one minute in restricted visibility?
answers: A vessel at anchor of less than 100 metres in length.
A vessel at anchor of 100 metres or more in length.
A vessel being towed, or the last manned vessel of a tow, underway.
A power-driven vessel underway that has stopped her engines and is making no way through the water.

explanation.de: Nach COLREG Regel 35(g) läutet ein vor Anker liegendes Fahrzeug von weniger als 100 m Länge bei verminderter Sicht mindestens jede Minute etwa 5 Sekunden lang rasch die Glocke. Ein Fahrzeug von 100 m oder mehr Länge (Antwort b) schlägt zusätzlich nach dem Glockenläuten einen Gong. Ein Maschinenfahrzeug ohne Fahrt (Antwort d) gibt zwei lange und einen kurzen Ton, kein Glockenläuten.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 35(g), a vessel at anchor of less than 100 metres in length rings the bell rapidly for about 5 seconds at intervals of not more than one minute in restricted visibility. A vessel of 100 metres or more (answer b) also sounds a gong aft after the bell. A power-driven vessel making no way (answer d) sounds two prolonged and one short blast — not a bell.
explanation.memoryAid: Anchor + short = bell only; anchor + long = bell AND gong.

en.question: Which vessel, in restricted visibility, rings the bell rapidly for approximately 5 seconds and immediately afterwards strikes the gong rapidly for approximately 5 seconds, at intervals of not more than one minute?
answers: A vessel at anchor of 100 metres or more in length.
A vessel at anchor of less than 100 metres in length.
A vessel being towed, or the last manned vessel in a tow, underway.
A power-driven vessel underway that has stopped her engines and has no way through the water.

explanation.de: Ein vor Anker liegendes Fahrzeug ab 100 m Länge muss in Sichtbehinderung im Vorschiff die Glocke und im Achterschiff den Gong läuten, um seine gesamte Ausdehnung anzuzeigen. Kürzere Ankerlieger (unter 100 m) geben nur das Glockensignal ohne anschließenden Gong. Maschinenfahrzeuge und Schleppverbände verwenden stattdessen Schallsignale mit Nebelhorn.
explanation.en: A vessel at anchor of 100 metres or more in length must sound the bell rapidly in the fore part and immediately afterwards strike the gong rapidly in the after part, to signal its full length to approaching traffic. Vessels under 100 metres at anchor use only the bell signal without a gong. Power-driven vessels and tows use whistle (horn) signals in restricted visibility instead.
explanation.memoryAid: 100+ metres = bell AND gong — one signal for each end of a long vessel.

en.question: What additional sound signal may any vessel at anchor give in restricted visibility to indicate its position to an approaching vessel?
answers: One short, one prolonged, and one short blast on the whistle (· — ·).
At least every two minutes a powerful sound signal that cannot be confused with the prescribed signals.
At least every two minutes three successive blasts on the whistle: one prolonged followed by two short (— · ·).
At least every two minutes three successive blasts on the whistle: two prolonged followed by one short (— — ·).

explanation.de: Ein Ankerlieger darf bei unsichtigem Wetter zusätzlich zu den vorgeschriebenen Glockensignalen das Pfiffensignal kurz-lang-kurz (· — ·) geben, um einem sich nähernden Fahrzeug seinen Standort anzuzeigen. Dieses optionale Zusatzsignal ist in der KVR (COLREG) Regel 35(g) geregelt. Die Antworten b, c und d beschreiben entweder falsche Signalfolgen oder nicht vorgesehene Signaltypen.
explanation.en: An anchored vessel may, in addition to the prescribed bell signals, optionally sound the whistle signal short-prolonged-short (· — ·) to indicate its position to an approaching vessel in restricted visibility. This optional additional signal is provided for in COLREG Rule 35(g). Options b, c, and d describe either incorrect signal patterns or signal types not prescribed for this purpose.
explanation.memoryAid: S-O-S shape: Short–lOng–Short = anchored vessel saying 'I'm Over here!'

en.question: How can you determine whether the risk of collision exists?
answers: When the distance to the other vessel is decreasing and the bearing is not changing, or not changing appreciably.
When the distance to the other vessel is decreasing and the course is not changing, or not changing appreciably.
When the distance to the other vessel is decreasing and the compass bearing is changing.
When the distance to the other vessel is decreasing and the course is changing.

explanation.de: Gemäß KVR Regel 7 besteht Kollisionsgefahr, wenn sich bei abnehmendem Abstand die Peilung zum anderen Fahrzeug nicht (oder kaum) ändert — die Fahrzeuge sind dann auf stetem Kollisionskurs. Eine sich ändernde Peilung (Option c) bedeutet in der Regel, dass die Fahrzeuge aneinander vorbeikommen. Kursänderungen (Optionen b/d) sind für diese Beurteilung nicht maßgeblich.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 7, risk of collision exists if the compass bearing to an approaching vessel does not change (or changes only slightly) while the distance decreases — this means the vessels are on a steady collision course. A changing bearing (option c) generally indicates the vessels will pass clear of each other. Course changes (options b/d) are irrelevant to this assessment.
explanation.memoryAid: Steady bearing, decreasing range = danger (SBDR rule).

en.question: Two sailing vessels in sight of one another are approaching in open waters or outside a fairway in such a way that a risk of collision exists. Which vessel must give way to the other if both have the wind on the same side?
answers: The windward vessel must give way to the leeward vessel.
The leeward vessel must give way to the windward vessel.
The vessel that has the wind on the port side.
The vessel that has the wind on the starboard side.

explanation.de: Wenn zwei Segelfahrzeuge den Wind von derselben Seite haben, muss das luvwärtige (dem Wind zugewandte) Fahrzeug dem leewärtigen (vom Wind abgewandten) Fahrzeug ausweichen (COLREG Regel 12a(ii)). Das leewärtige Fahrzeug hat Vorfahrt, weil es durch das luvwärtige Fahrzeug im Wind abgedeckt werden könnte und weniger Manövrierfähigkeit besitzt.
