Antworten c und d sind falsch, da sie die Regel für Fahrzeuge mit Wind von verschiedenen Seiten beschreiben.
explanation.en: When two sailing vessels have the wind on the same side, the windward vessel (closer to the wind) must give way to the leeward vessel (COLREG Rule 12(a)(ii)). The leeward vessel has right of way because it may be blanketed by the windward vessel and has less room to manoeuvre. Answers c and d are incorrect as they describe the rule that applies when vessels have the wind on different sides.
explanation.memoryAid: Windward gives way: the vessel UP in the wind steps DOWN for the leeward vessel.

en.question: How must two power-driven vessels in sight of one another, approaching each other on reciprocal or nearly reciprocal courses, act to avoid the risk of collision?
answers: Each vessel shall alter her course to starboard.
Each vessel shall alter her course to port.
The windward vessel must give way to the leeward vessel.
The leeward vessel must give way to the windward vessel.

explanation.de: Gemäß KVR Regel 14 (Entgegenkommende Fahrzeuge) müssen beide Maschinenfahrzeuge ihren Kurs nach Steuerbord ändern, sodass jedes Fahrzeug an der Backbordseite des anderen vorbeifährt. Eine Kursänderung nach Backbord (Antwort b) wäre gefährlich. Die Antworten c und d betreffen Segelfahrzeuge und sind hier nicht anwendbar.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 14 (head-on situation), when two power-driven vessels are meeting on reciprocal or nearly reciprocal courses, both vessels must alter course to starboard so that each passes on the port side of the other. Altering to port (answer b) would be dangerous as it could bring the vessels together. Answers c and d describe sailing vessel rules, which do not apply here.
explanation.memoryAid: Head-on? Both go RIGHT — starboard keeps ships apart, never tight.

en.question: How must a power-driven vessel in open waters or outside a fairway behave towards a sailing vessel in sight when there is a possibility of danger of collision?
answers: The power-driven vessel must give way.
The power-driven vessel must maintain course and speed.
The power-driven vessel must reduce its speed.
The power-driven vessel must manoeuvre carefully until the danger has passed.

explanation.de: Nach COLREG Regel 18 muss ein Maschinenfahrzeug gegenüber einem Segelfahrzeug ausweichen — es ist das ausweichpflichtige Fahrzeug. Das Segelfahrzeug ist das kurshaltepflichtige Fahrzeug und muss Kurs und Geschwindigkeit beibehalten (Antwort b wäre die Pflicht des Segelfahrzeugs). Nur die Geschwindigkeit zu verringern (c) oder vorsichtig zu manövrieren (d) genügt der Ausweichpflicht nicht.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 18, a power-driven vessel must give way to a sailing vessel — it is the give-way vessel. The sailing vessel is the stand-on vessel and must maintain course and speed (answer b describes the stand-on vessel's duty). Merely reducing speed (c) or manoeuvring carefully (d) does not fulfil the obligation to give way.
explanation.memoryAid: Power gives way to sail — the engine has the burden.

en.question: How must a power-driven vessel in open waters or outside a fairway behave towards a vessel not under command that is in sight, when there is a possibility of risk of collision?
answers: The power-driven vessel must give way.
The power-driven vessel must maintain its course and speed.
The power-driven vessel must alter its course to starboard.
The power-driven vessel must reduce its speed.

explanation.de: Gemäß KVR Regel 18 muss ein Maschinenfahrzeug einem manövrierunfähigen Fahrzeug ausweichen, da dieses nicht in der Lage ist, selbst auszuweichen. Das bloße Verringern der Fahrt oder eine Kursänderung nach Steuerbord allein sind keine ausreichenden Maßnahmen – die Pflicht lautet ausdrücklich 'ausweichen', also alle notwendigen Maßnahmen zu ergreifen, um einen sicheren Abstand herzustellen.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 18, a power-driven vessel must keep out of the way of a vessel not under command, because that vessel is unable to manoeuvre to avoid a collision. Simply reducing speed or turning to starboard alone are not sufficient — the obligation is specifically to 'give way', meaning to take all necessary action to maintain a safe distance.
explanation.memoryAid: Not Under Command = Not able to dodge — so YOU must give way.

en.question: How must a power-driven vessel in open waters or outside the fairway behave towards a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre that is in sight, when there is a possibility of the risk of collision?
answers: The power-driven vessel must give way.
The power-driven vessel must maintain her course and speed.
The power-driven vessel must alter her course to starboard.
The power-driven vessel must reduce her speed.

explanation.de: Gemäß KVR (COLREG) Regel 18 muss ein Maschinenfahrzeug gegenüber einem manövrierbehinderten Fahrzeug ausweichen, da dieses nicht in der Lage ist, selbst auszuweichen. Die bloße Kursänderung nach Steuerbord (c) oder Fahrtverringerung (d) wären unvollständige Maßnahmen — die Pflicht lautet ausdrücklich 'ausweichen', also dem anderen Fahrzeug den Weg freizumachen.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 18, a power-driven vessel must keep out of the way of a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, because that vessel cannot manoeuvre freely to avoid a collision. Simply altering course to starboard (c) or reducing speed (d) are incomplete actions — the obligation is explicitly to give way, meaning to take whatever action is necessary to keep clear.
explanation.memoryAid: RAM (Restricted in Ability to Manoeuvre) beats engine power — always give way to a vessel that can't move freely.

en.question: How must a power-driven vessel behave in open waters or outside a fairway towards a fishing vessel in sight, when the possibility of a risk of collision exists?
answers: The power-driven vessel must give way.
The power-driven vessel must maintain course and speed.
The power-driven vessel must alter course to starboard.
The power-driven vessel must manoeuvre carefully until the danger has passed.

explanation.de: Gemäß KVR Regel 18 muss ein Maschinenfahrzeug gegenüber einem fischenden Fahrzeug (das mit Netzen, Leinen oder Schleppnetzen fischt) ausweichen, wenn Kollisionsgefahr besteht. Kurs und Geschwindigkeit beibehalten (b) ist die Pflicht des Kurshaltefahrzeugs — also das Gegenteil. Das Ausweichen nach Steuerbord (c) ist keine allgemeine Regel für diese Situation, und das vorsichtige Manövrieren (d) gilt für eingeschränkte Sichtverhältnisse nach Regel 19, nicht für Sichtfahrt.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 18, a power-driven vessel underway must keep out of the way of a fishing vessel (one engaged in fishing with nets, lines, or trawls). The give-way obligation applies whenever there is a risk of collision. Simply maintaining course and speed (b) is the stand-on vessel's duty — the opposite of what is required here. Altering course to starboard (c) is a specific collision-avoidance action but is not the general rule that applies; and cautious manoeuvring (d) describes the restricted-visibility rule (Rule 19), not the in-sight rule.
explanation.memoryAid: Fishing vessels have priority over power: F beats P in open water.

en.question: How must a sailing vessel behave in open waters or outside a fairway toward a vessel engaged in fishing that is in sight, when the possibility of a risk of collision exists?
answers: The sailing vessel must give way.
The sailing vessel must alter course to starboard.
The sailing vessel must not impede the safe passage of the fishing vessel.
The sailing vessel must initially maintain its course and speed.

explanation.de: Gemäß Regel 18 KVR muss ein Segelfahrzeug einem fischenden Fahrzeug ausweichen. Diese Pflicht gilt im freien Seeraum oder außerhalb des Fahrwassers, sobald die Möglichkeit einer Kollisionsgefahr besteht. Eine bloße Kursänderung nach Steuerbord (Antwort b) ist hier keine vorgeschriebene Maßnahme — das Ausweichfahrzeug muss frühzeitig und ausreichend ausweichen.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 18, a sailing vessel must keep out of the way of a vessel engaged in fishing. This applies in open waters outside a fairway whenever a risk of collision exists. Simply altering course to starboard (answer b) is not a prescribed rule here — the give-way vessel must take early and substantial action to keep clear.
explanation.memoryAid: Fishing > Sailing in the COLREG hierarchy: 'Fish beat sails.'

en.question: How must you conduct yourself with respect to this vessel?
answers: You must not impede the safe passage of the vessel.
The vessel must be passed on the starboard side.
Avoid suction and wash.
Maintain course and speed.

explanation.de: Bestimmte Fahrzeuge – insbesondere solche, die aufgrund ihres Tiefgangs oder ihrer Größe nur einen bestimmten Fahrweg nutzen können (z. B. tiefgangsbeschränkte Fahrzeuge nach KVR/COLREG Regel 18 bzw. 9) – genießen das Recht auf ungehinderte sichere Durchfahrt. Andere Fahrzeuge dürfen diese sichere Durchfahrt nicht behindern. Das Beibehalten von Kurs und Geschwindigkeit (d) oder das Passieren an Steuerbord (b) sind keine allgemein gültigen Vorschriften für diese Situation.
explanation.en: Certain vessels – particularly those restricted by their draught or size to a specific channel (e.g. vessels constrained by draught or vessels in a narrow channel under COLREG Rules 9/18) – have a right to safe passage. Other vessels must not impede that safe passage. Maintaining course and speed (d) or passing on the starboard side (b) are not the applicable general rules in this context.
explanation.memoryAid: If they're big and stuck in the channel, stay out of their way — don't impede, don't interfere.

en.question: How must you behave towards this vessel?
answers: The vessel's safe passage must not be impeded.
The vessel must be passed on the starboard side.
Avoid suction and wash.
Maintain course and speed.

explanation.de: Bestimmte Fahrzeuge – wie tiefgangsbeschränkte Fahrzeuge oder Fahrzeuge, die im Fahrwasser beschränkt manövrierfähig sind – dürfen in ihrer sicheren Durchfahrt nicht behindert werden (KVR Regel 9, 18). Das bloße Passieren an Steuerbord oder das Beibehalten von Kurs und Geschwindigkeit ist keine ausreichende Pflicht; die aktive Nichtbehinderung steht im Vordergrund.
explanation.en: Certain vessels – such as vessels restricted in their ability to manoeuvre or constrained by their draught – must not be impeded in their safe passage (COLREG Rules 9, 18). Simply passing on the starboard side or maintaining course and speed does not fulfil this obligation; the primary duty is to actively avoid impeding the vessel.
explanation.memoryAid: Not impede = actively keep clear, not just hold course.

en.question: How does the stand-on vessel behave towards a give-way vessel before initiating the last-moment manoeuvre?
answers: Maintain course and speed initially, and pay particular attention to the give-way vessel.
Adjust course or speed, and pay particular attention to the give-way vessel.
Alter course to starboard, reduce speed, and pay particular attention to the give-way vessel.
Alter course to starboard, maintain speed initially, and pay particular attention to the give-way vessel.

explanation.de: Der Kurshaltepflichtige muss gemäß KVR (COLREG Regel 17) zunächst Kurs und Geschwindigkeit beibehalten, damit das ausweichpflichtige Fahrzeug ein vorhersehbares Ziel hat und sein Ausweichmanöver planen kann. Erst wenn eine Kollision durch das Manöver des Ausweichpflichtigen allein nicht mehr vermieden werden kann, darf der Kurshaltepflichtige das Manöver des letzten Augenblicks einleiten. Änderungen von Kurs oder Geschwindigkeit vorher (Antworten b, c, d) würden die Situation unberechenbar machen.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 17, the stand-on vessel must initially maintain its course and speed so that the give-way vessel has a predictable target and can plan its avoiding action. Only when collision can no longer be avoided by the give-way vessel's action alone may the stand-on vessel take the last-moment manoeuvre. Prematurely altering course or speed (options b, c, d) would make the situation unpredictable for the give-way vessel.
explanation.memoryAid: Stand-on = Stay on — hold course and speed until the last moment.

en.question: How must a give-way vessel behave towards a stand-on vessel?
answers: The give-way manoeuvre must be carried out early, decisively, and in a manner that is clearly apparent.
The course must be adjusted step by step as the stand-on vessel is approached, so that the other vessel's stern is safely passed.
A last-moment manoeuvre is to be executed. The vessel must give way in whatever manner is most conducive to avoiding a collision.
Speed must be reduced to the minimum required to maintain steerage; in case of doubt, the vessel must stop completely.

explanation.de: Nach den Kollisionsverhütungsregeln (COLREG, Regel 16) muss das ausweichpflichtige Fahrzeug rechtzeitig, großzügig und eindeutig manövrieren, damit der Kurshalter sicher erkennen kann, dass ausgewichen wird. Schrittweise Kursanpassungen (Antwort b) sind gefährlich, weil sie die Absicht unklar lassen. Das 'Manöver des letzten Augenblicks' (Antwort c) beschreibt die Pflicht des Kurshaltepflichtigen nach Regel 17, nicht des Ausweichpflichtigen.
explanation.en: Under the COLREGs (Rule 16), the give-way vessel must take early, large, and unambiguous action so that the stand-on vessel can clearly see that avoiding action is being taken. Gradual course adjustments (answer b) are dangerous because they leave the intentions unclear. The 'last-moment manoeuvre' (answer c) refers to the stand-on vessel's obligation under Rule 17, not the give-way vessel's.
explanation.memoryAid: Give way: Early, Big, and Obvious — leave no doubt you're moving out.

en.question: How must an overtaking vessel behave?
answers: It must keep out of the way of the vessel being overtaken.
It must maintain the greatest possible distance from the overtaken vessel and avoid suction and wash.
It must not impede the safe passage of the vessel being overtaken.
It must give a sound signal before overtaking in order to obtain the consent of the vessel being overtaken.

explanation.de: Gemäß KVR (COLREG) Regel 13 muss ein überholendes Fahrzeug dem überholten Fahrzeug ausweichen und so weit von ihm entfernt bleiben, bis es sicher vorbei und klar ist. Die anderen Antworten beschreiben entweder Binnenschifffahrtsregeln (b), die Pflichten des langsameren Fahrzeugs (c) oder ein nicht vorgesehenes Verfahren auf See (d).
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 13, an overtaking vessel must keep out of the way of the vessel being overtaken and remain clear until she is finally past and clear. Option (b) reflects inland waterway rules, option (c) describes the duty of the vessel being overtaken rather than the overtaker, and option (d) describes a sound-signal consent procedure that does not apply at sea.
explanation.memoryAid: The overtaker is always the 'give-way' vessel — she must stay clear until completely past.

en.question: How must you act when, in restricted visibility, you hear the sound signal of another vessel apparently forward of your beam?
answers: You must also sound a signal and reduce speed to the minimum at which you can still maintain steerage. If necessary, take all way off. In any case, manoeuvre with caution until the danger of collision is past.
You must also sound a signal and take early, substantial, and clearly recognisable avoiding action.
You must sound at least five short blasts on the whistle and carry out the last-moment manoeuvre, manoeuvring in whatever way is most helpful to avoid a collision.
You must also sound a signal and maintain course and speed until the other vessel comes into sight. Then assess the collision-avoidance situation under the COLREGs and act accordingly.

explanation.de: Nach KVR Regel 19(d) muss ein Fahrzeug bei verminderter Sicht, das vorlicher als querab ein Schallsignal eines anderen Fahrzeugs hört, die Fahrt auf ein Minimum reduzieren und vorsichtig manövrieren. Kurs und Geschwindigkeit beizubehalten (d) wäre falsch; aktives Ausweichen (b) ist ohne Sichtkontakt nicht vorgeschrieben.
explanation.en: COLREG Rule 19(d) requires that when a vessel hears, apparently forward of the beam, the fog signal of another vessel, she shall reduce speed to the minimum needed for steerage and manoeuvre with caution until the danger of collision is past. Maintaining course and speed (d) or blindly taking avoiding action (b) without visual contact would be incorrect.
explanation.memoryAid: Fog signal ahead = Slow down, sound back, stay alert — don't race toward what you can't see.

en.question: How should the stand-on vessel act when it determines that the give-way vessel is not fulfilling its obligation to give way and the danger of an imminent collision is at hand?
answers: You sound at least five short blasts on the whistle and carry out the 'last-moment manoeuvre'. You must manoeuvre in whatever way is most helpful to avoid a collision.

You sound a sound signal (four short blasts) and reduce speed to the extent that manoeuvrability is still maintained. If necessary, you stop completely. In any case, you manoeuvre cautiously until the danger of collision has passed.
You sound at least five short blasts on the whistle and reduce speed to avoid suction and wash.
You maintain course and speed for the time being and pay particular attention to the give-way vessel.

explanation.de: Gemäß KVR Regel 17 darf der Kurshalter zunächst Kurs und Geschwindigkeit beibehalten, muss aber handeln, wenn die Kollision unmittelbar droht. Das 'Manöver des letzten Augenblicks' ist dann mit mindestens fünf kurzen Tönen (Achtungssignal) einzuleiten und so durchzuführen, wie es zur Vermeidung des Zusammenstoßes am dienlichsten ist. Vier kurze Töne (Antwort b) sind kein standardisiertes COLREG-Signal.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 17, the stand-on vessel may initially maintain course and speed, but must take action when collision becomes imminent. The 'last-moment manoeuvre' must then be initiated with at least five short blasts (the danger/warning signal) and executed in whatever manner best avoids the collision. Four short blasts (answer b) is not a standardised COLREG signal.
explanation.memoryAid: Five short blasts = danger signal; when all else fails, the stand-on vessel acts to save both.

en.question: What is the meaning of the following sound signal? (at least [5 short blasts])
answers: A vessel required to give way is being reminded of its obligation to keep clear.
General danger and warning signal.
Keep-away signal: explosion hazard due to dangerous cargo. Leave the danger area immediately. Avoid fire and ignition sparks.
Waterway closed. Proceeding further is prohibited; stop immediately.

explanation.de: Mindestens fünf kurze Töne sind das Misstrauens- oder Warnsignal nach KVR (Regel 34d): Es wird eingesetzt, wenn ein ausweichpflichtiges Fahrzeug seiner Pflicht nicht nachzukommen scheint. Das allgemeine Gefahrensignal (Antwort b) besteht aus einer anderen Signalfolge, und das Bleib-Weg-Signal (Antwort c) ist ein spezielles Funksignal, kein einfaches Schallsignal.
explanation.en: At least five short blasts constitute the doubt/warning signal under COLREG Rule 34(d): it is used when a stand-on vessel is in doubt that a give-way vessel is taking sufficient action to avoid collision. The general danger signal (answer b) uses a different sequence, and the keep-away signal (answer c) is a specific VHF/radio-based signal, not this simple sound signal.
explanation.memoryAid: Five (or more) short blasts = 'Hey! You must give way!' — doubt that the other vessel is doing its job.

en.question: What is the meaning of the following sound signal?
answers: A vessel at anchor is alerting an approaching vessel to a dangerous approach.
The vessel's engine is running astern.
Protected installation; reduce speed, avoid suction and wash.
A power-driven vessel that has stopped its engines and is making no way through the water.

explanation.de: Das Signal — • • (ein langer Ton, zwei kurze Töne) wird von einem Ankerliegenden abgegeben, um ein sich näherndes Fahrzeug auf eine gefährliche Annäherung aufmerksam zu machen (Regel 35(g) KVR). Das Signal • • (zwei kurze Töne) bedeutet dagegen 'Maschine rückwärts', und ••• (drei kurze Töne) steht für ein Fahrzeug ohne Fahrt durchs Wasser.
explanation.en: The signal — • • (one prolonged blast followed by two short blasts) is sounded by a vessel at anchor to warn an approaching vessel of a dangerous close-quarters situation (COLREG Rule 35(g)). By contrast, two short blasts (• •) means 'engine going astern', and three short blasts (• • •) indicates a vessel making no way through the water.
explanation.memoryAid: Long-short-short at anchor = 'Watch out — too close!' (one long warning, two short sharps).

en.question: What must be observed when using a traffic separation scheme?
answers: Proceed in the appropriate lane in the general direction of traffic flow for that lane; keep as clear as possible of the traffic separation zone/line; in general, join or leave the lane at its ends; when joining or leaving from the side, do so at as small an angle as possible to the general direction of traffic flow.

Proceed in the appropriate lane to the left of the separation zone in the direction of traffic flow; keep as close as possible to the separation zone/line; in general, join or leave the lane at its ends; when joining or leaving from the side, do so at as nearly a right angle as possible to the general direction of traffic flow.

The use of traffic separation schemes is not permitted for sailing vessels or for power-driven vessels under 20 m in length. These vessels shall keep as clear as possible of traffic separation schemes and must make it clear by their course that they are not using a traffic separation scheme.

Vessels proceeding in the appropriate lane in the general direction of traffic flow must keep as clear as possible of the separation zone/line and have right of way over all vessels entering or crossing a traffic separation scheme.

explanation.de: Nach COLREG Regel 10 müssen Fahrzeuge in einem Verkehrstrennungsgebiet (VTG) dem Einbahnweg in allgemeiner Verkehrsrichtung folgen, so weit wie möglich von der Trennzone freihalten und möglichst an den Enden ein- oder auslaufen. Seitliches Ein- oder Auslaufen soll in möglichst kleinem Winkel erfolgen, damit der Querverkehr minimiert wird. Antwort b ist falsch, da man nicht links von der Trennzone fahren oder einen rechten Winkel beim seitlichen Einlaufen anstreben soll; Antwort d ist falsch, da Fahrzeuge im VTG keine grundsätzliche Vorfahrt haben.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 10, vessels in a traffic separation scheme (TSS) must proceed in the appropriate lane in the general direction of traffic flow, keep as clear as possible of the separation zone, and normally join or leave at the ends. When joining or leaving from the side, the angle to the general traffic direction should be as small as possible to minimise cross-traffic. Answer b is wrong because vessels should not keep close to the separation zone or join at a right angle; answer d is wrong because vessels in a TSS do not automatically have right of way over all other vessels.
explanation.memoryAid: Small angle in, big distance from the line — TSS rules in a line!

en.question: What must be observed when crossing a traffic separation scheme?
answers: Crossing is to be avoided if possible. If crossing is necessary, it must be done with the vessel's heading at as close to a right angle as possible to the general direction of traffic flow. The heading of the crossing vessel must form a right angle to the general direction of traffic flow even when the vessel is being set by wind or current.

Crossing is to be avoided if possible. If crossing is necessary, it must be done with a true course at as close to a right angle as possible to the general direction of traffic flow. The true course of the crossing vessel must form a right angle to the general direction of traffic flow even when the vessel is being set by wind or current.

Crossing traffic separation schemes is prohibited for sailing vessels and for power-driven vessels under 20 m in length. These vessels must keep as clear as possible of the ends of the traffic separation scheme and must make clear by their course that they are not crossing a traffic separation scheme.

Crossing is to be avoided if possible. If crossing is necessary, it must be done with the vessel's heading at as acute an angle as possible to the general direction of traffic flow. The heading of the crossing vessel must also form as acute an angle as possible to the general direction of traffic flow even when the vessel is being set by wind or current.

explanation.de: Gemäß COLREG Regel 10 muss ein Fahrzeug, das ein Verkehrstrennungsgebiet quert, dies möglichst mit der Kielrichtung (dem Schiffskörper) im rechten Winkel zur Verkehrsrichtung tun – nicht mit dem rechtweisenden Kurs. Wenn das Schiff durch Wind oder Strom versetzt wird, bleibt die Kielrichtung (nicht der Kurs über Grund) maßgebend, damit andere Verkehrsteilnehmer die Absicht des Fahrzeugs klar erkennen können. Antwort b ist falsch, weil sie den rechtweisenden Kurs statt die Kielrichtung nennt; Antwort d ist falsch, weil ein spitzer (nicht rechter) Winkel gefordert wird.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 10, a vessel crossing a traffic separation scheme must do so with its heading (the ship's fore-and-aft axis) as close to a right angle as practicable to the general direction of traffic flow — not its true course made good. Even if wind or current sets the vessel off track, the heading (not the track over ground) must still show the right angle so that the vessel's intention is clearly apparent to others. Answer b is wrong because it refers to true course rather than heading; answer d is wrong because it demands an acute angle instead of a right angle.
explanation.memoryAid: KEEL at 90°: point your bow square across, let the current do what it will.

en.question: In which regulation are the rules for navigating traffic separation schemes found?
answers: In the Collision Regulations (COLREGs).
In the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (German Inland Coastal Waters Ordinance).
In both the Collision Regulations and the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung.
In the 'Notices of the Generaldirektion Wasserstraßen und Schifffahrt (GDWS)'.

explanation.de: Die Regeln für das Befahren von Verkehrstrennungsgebieten sind in Regel 10 der Kollisionsverhütungsregeln (KVR / COLREGs) festgelegt. Die Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung gilt für deutsche Küstengewässer, enthält aber nicht die grundlegenden Regeln zu Verkehrstrennungsgebieten. Die GDWS-Bekanntmachungen sind behördliche Informationen, keine verbindlichen Regelwerke für diesen Zweck.
explanation.en: The rules for navigating traffic separation schemes are set out in Rule 10 of the COLREGs (Collision Regulations). The Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung applies to German coastal waters but does not contain the fundamental rules on traffic separation schemes. GDWS notices are administrative publications, not the binding ruleset for this purpose.
explanation.memoryAid: Rule 10 of COLREGs = Traffic Separation Scheme rules — one rule, one source.

en.question: How must a power-driven vessel, when in danger of collision in a one-way lane of a traffic separation scheme, behave towards a power-driven vessel that is crossing the lane from starboard?
answers: It must give way to the other vessel.
It must not impede the safe passage of the power-driven vessel.
It must pay particular attention to the crossing vessel.
It must carry out a last-minute manoeuvre.

explanation.de: Obwohl ein Fahrzeug, das einen Einbahnweg eines Verkehrstrennungsgebietes quert, grundsätzlich dem im Einbahnweg fahrenden Fahrzeug nicht in den Weg treten darf (COLREG Regel 10), bleibt die Ausweichpflicht nach Regel 15 (Kurse, die sich kreuzen) bestehen: Kommt das querende Fahrzeug von Steuerbord, ist das Fahrzeug im Einbahnweg das Geberfahrzeug und muss ausweichen. Die Regel 10 hebt die allgemeinen Ausweichregeln nicht auf.
explanation.en: Although a vessel crossing a traffic separation lane must in principle not impede vessels following the lane (COLREG Rule 10), the crossing rules under Rule 15 still apply: when the crossing vessel approaches from starboard, the vessel in the lane is the give-way vessel and must yield. Rule 10 does not override the general steering and sailing rules.
explanation.memoryAid: Starboard = right of way — even inside a TSS lane, the vessel on your starboard side has priority.

en.question: How must a sailing vessel behave when crossing a traffic separation scheme with respect to a power-driven vessel proceeding along a traffic lane in the general direction of traffic flow?
answers: It must not impede the safe passage of the power-driven vessel.
It is subject to the obligation to maintain course and speed.
It must wait. All vessels following the traffic lane have right of way.
It has right of way. All vessels following the traffic lane must wait.

explanation.de: Gemäß COLREG Regel 10 darf ein Fahrzeug, das ein Verkehrstrennungsgebiet quert, die sichere Durchfahrt von Fahrzeugen, die einem Einbahnweg folgen, nicht behindern – unabhängig davon, ob es sich um ein Segel- oder Motorfahrzeug handelt. Die Kurshalte- und Ausweichpflicht nach Regel 12 (Segelfahrzeuge untereinander) oder Regel 18 (Segelfahrzeug hat Vorrang vor Maschinenfahrzeug) tritt hier zurück. Antwort b ist falsch, weil das Segelfahrzeug gerade nicht passiv bleiben darf, sondern aktiv sicherstellen muss, dass es nicht behindert.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 10, a vessel crossing a traffic separation scheme must not impede the safe passage of vessels following a traffic lane, regardless of vessel type. This overrides the general priority of sailing vessels over power-driven vessels (Rule 18) in this specific context. Answer b is incorrect because the sailing vessel is not simply required to hold course — it must actively avoid hindering the power-driven vessel.
explanation.memoryAid: Crossing traffic lanes? You're the guest — don't block the highway traffic.

en.question: How must vessels of less than 20 metres in length or sailing vessels behave in traffic separation schemes?
answers: They must not impede the safe passage of a power-driven vessel following a traffic lane.
They are considered small craft and are not permitted to navigate in traffic separation schemes.
They are considered small craft and may only navigate in traffic separation schemes during daylight hours and in good visibility.
They may navigate in the separation zone so as not to obstruct through traffic.

explanation.de: Nach COLREG Regel 10(j) dürfen Fahrzeuge unter 20 m Länge und Segelfahrzeuge Verkehrstrennungsgebiete benutzen, müssen aber die sichere Durchfahrt eines dem Einbahnweg folgenden Maschinenfahrzeugs gewährleisten. Sie gelten nicht pauschal als 'Kleinfahrzeuge' im Sinne eines generellen Verbots, und das Befahren der Trennzone (Antwort d) ist grundsätzlich verboten, nicht erlaubt.
explanation.en: Under COLREG Rule 10(j), vessels under 20 m in length and sailing vessels may use traffic separation schemes but must not impede the safe passage of a power-driven vessel following a traffic lane. They are not categorically banned from TSS (answers b and c are wrong), and navigating in the separation zone itself (answer d) is prohibited, not permitted.
explanation.memoryAid: Small sail or short vessel: you may enter, but never hinder the big ships in their lane.

en.question: What type of vessel is this, and what must be observed?
answers: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, engaged in dredging or underwater operations, and thereby obstructing navigation. She must be passed on the side where two black diamonds are arranged vertically one above the other.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, obstructing navigation. She must be passed on the side where two black balls are arranged vertically one above the other.

A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, engaged in dredging or underwater operations, and thereby obstructing navigation. She must be passed on the side that lies to the right in your direction of travel.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, engaged in dredging or underwater operations, and thereby obstructing navigation. She may not be passed on either side.

explanation.de: Ein Fahrzeug, das baggert oder Unterwasserarbeiten ausführt und die Schifffahrt behindert, zeigt tagsüber an der Seite, an der passiert werden darf, zwei schwarze Rauten (Rhomben) senkrecht übereinander. Antwort b ist falsch, da Bälle das falsche Tageszeichen sind; Antwort c ist falsch, da die passierbare Seite durch das Zeichen – nicht durch die eigene Fahrtrichtung – bestimmt wird; Antwort d ist falsch, weil das Fahrzeug an der mit Rauten gekennzeichneten Seite passiert werden darf.
explanation.en: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre while dredging or conducting underwater operations that obstruct navigation displays two black diamond (rhombus) shapes vertically one above the other on the side that is safe to pass. Answer b is wrong because balls are the incorrect daymark; answer c is wrong because the passable side is determined by the vessel's signals, not your heading; answer d is wrong because passage is permitted on the diamond-marked side.
explanation.memoryAid: Two diamonds stacked = safe to pass on that side — diamonds mark the 'diamond lane'.

en.question: What type of vessel is this and what must be observed?
answers: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, underway, engaged in dredging or underwater operations, and not obstructing navigation. She is to be passed on the side that lies to the right in the direction of travel.

A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, underway, engaged in dredging or underwater operations, and obstructing navigation. She is to be passed on the side that lies to the left in the direction of travel.
A vessel not under command, underway, engaged in dredging or underwater operations, and obstructing navigation. She is to be passed on the side that lies to the right in the direction of travel.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, underway, engaged in dredging or underwater operations, and obstructing navigation. She may be passed on either side.

explanation.de: Ein manövrierbehindertes Fahrzeug, das baggert oder Unterwasserarbeiten ausführt, ohne die Schifffahrt zu behindern, zeigt zwei rote Rundumlichter (übereinander) sowie die üblichen Lichter für Fahrt durchs Wasser – aber keine zusätzlichen grünen Lichter. Da es die Schifffahrt nicht behindert, darf es von der Seite passiert werden, die in Fahrtrichtung rechts liegt (d. h. auf der Seite, auf der keine Gefahr besteht). Antworten b und d sind falsch, weil sie fälschlich eine Behinderung der Schifffahrt angeben; Antwort c ist falsch, weil das Fahrzeug manövrierBEHINDERT, nicht manövrierUNFÄHIG ist.
explanation.en: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre while dredging or performing underwater work, but NOT obstructing navigation, displays two all-round red lights (in a vertical line) along with her normal underway lights — but no additional green lights. Because she is not obstructing traffic, other vessels pass on the side to the right in the direction of travel (the safe, unobstructed side). Answers b and d are wrong because they incorrectly state the vessel is obstructing navigation; answer c is wrong because the vessel is restricted in ability to manoeuvre, not 'not under command'.
explanation.memoryAid: No green lights = no obstruction = pass on the GREEN (starboard/right) side.

en.question: What type of vessel is this and what must be observed?
answers: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, not making way through the water, engaged in dredging or underwater operations and thereby obstructing navigation. She must be passed on the side where two green all-round lights are arranged vertically one above the other.

A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, not making way through the water, and thereby obstructing navigation. She must be passed on the side where two red all-round lights are arranged vertically one above the other.

A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, not making way through the water, engaged in dredging or underwater operations and thereby obstructing navigation. She must be passed on the side that lies to the left in the direction of travel.

A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, not making way through the water, engaged in dredging or underwater operations and thereby obstructing navigation. She must be passed on the starboard side of the fairway (keep-to-starboard rule).

explanation.de: Ein manövrierbehindertes Fahrzeug, das baggert oder Unterwasserarbeiten ausführt und die Schifffahrt behindert, zeigt nach COLREG Regel 27 auf der freien (passierbaren) Seite zwei grüne Rundumlichter übereinander und auf der gesperrten Seite zwei rote Rundumlichter übereinander. Andere Fahrzeuge müssen daher auf der Seite passieren, an der die zwei grünen Lichter erscheinen. Antwort (b) ist falsch, weil zwei rote Lichter übereinander die gesperrte (nicht passierbare) Seite kennzeichnen.
explanation.en: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre while dredging or conducting underwater operations that obstruct navigation displays, under COLREG Rule 27, two green all-round lights vertically on the clear (passable) side and two red all-round lights vertically on the obstructed side. Other vessels must therefore pass on the side showing the two green lights. Answer (b) is wrong because two red lights indicate the obstructed side, not the safe passing side.
explanation.memoryAid: Green = Go (pass here); Red = Stop (obstructed side).

en.question: What type of vessel is this and what must be observed?
answers: Vessel carrying dangerous goods. Keep clear, smoking and open flames are prohibited.
Vessel in public service. It is permitted to deviate from traffic regulations.
Vessel in distress. Render assistance or request further help.
Vessel with a diver in operation. Keep a large distance.

explanation.de: Ein Fahrzeug mit gefährlichen Gütern führt tagsüber die rote Flagge 'B' des Internationalen Signalbuches oder nachts ein rotes Rundumlicht. Andere Fahrzeuge müssen Abstand halten, und Rauchen sowie offenes Feuer sind wegen Explosions- und Brandgefahr streng verboten. Die anderen Antworten beschreiben andere Signale: blaues Blinklicht für Behördenfahrzeuge, Notsignale oder die Alpha-Flagge für Taucherarbeiten.
explanation.en: A vessel carrying dangerous goods displays a red flag (flag 'B' of the International Code of Signals) by day or a red all-round light by night. All other vessels must keep clear, and smoking or open flames in the vicinity are strictly forbidden due to the risk of explosion or fire. The other options describe different signal displays (blue flashing light for public-service vessels, distress signals, or the Alpha flag for diving operations).
explanation.memoryAid: Red flag 'B' = Beware — Boom risk aboard!

en.question: Where is it defined which bodies of water are classified as sea waterways (Seeschifffahrtsstraßen)?
answers: Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (Sea Waterways Regulations) and Schifffahrtsordnung Emsmündung (Ems Estuary Navigation Order).
Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (Sea Waterways Regulations) and Kollisionsverhütungsregeln (COLREGs).
Kollisionsverhütungsregeln (COLREGs) and Schifffahrtsordnung Emsmündung (Ems Estuary Navigation Order).
Kollisionsverhütungsregeln (COLREGs) and Seeaufgabengesetz (Maritime Tasks Act).

explanation.de: Die Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO) legt fest, welche Gewässer als Seeschifffahrtsstraßen gelten, und regelt die Schifffahrt auf diesen Gewässern. Die Schifffahrtsordnung Emsmündung (EmsSchO) ergänzt dies für den Bereich der Emsmündung, der nicht vollständig unter die SeeSchStrO fällt. Die Kollisionsverhütungsregeln (KVR) gelten auf hoher See und enthalten keine Definition der deutschen Seeschifffahrtsstraßen.
explanation.en: The Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO) defines which waters are classified as German sea waterways and governs navigation on them. The Schifffahrtsordnung Emsmündung (EmsSchO) supplements this for the Ems Estuary area, which is not fully covered by the SeeSchStrO. The COLREGs apply on the high seas and do not define German sea waterways.
explanation.memoryAid: Two German-specific orders define German waters: SeeSchStrO for most sea waterways, EmsSchO for the Ems — COLREGs cover the open sea, not inland definitions.

en.question: What local special regulations exist in addition to the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO) and the Schifffahrtsordnung Emsmündung (EmsSchO), and what do they govern?
answers: The notices (Bekanntmachungen) of the Generaldirektion Wasserstraßen und Schifffahrt (GDWS), which contain special local provisions and provide guidance for the individual federal waterways (Seeschifffahrtsstraßen).

The Notices to Mariners (Nachrichten für Seefahrer, NfS), published by the Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency (BSH), and the Mariners' Notices (Bekanntmachungen für Seefahrer, BfS) issued by the locally responsible Waterways and Shipping Offices (WSÄ), which draw attention to all changes regarding buoyage, lighting, wrecks and shoals, as well as measures and events affecting navigation.

The notices of the Generaldirektion Wasserstraßen und Schifffahrt (GDWS) and the nautical publication 'Sicherheit auf dem Wasser' (Safety on the Water), published by the Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport Affairs (BMDV), containing important rules and tips for recreational boaters.

The Maritime Safety Investigation Act (Seesicherheitsuntersuchungsgesetz) and the Regulation on the Safety of Navigation (Verordnung über die Sicherung der Seefahrt), each containing important provisions on conduct following a collision on the respective federal waterways.

explanation.de: Die richtige Antwort ist (a): Die Bekanntmachungen der GDWS sind die offiziellen örtlichen Sondervorschriften, die ergänzend zur SeeSchStrO und EmsSchO besondere Regelungen und Hinweise für die einzelnen Seeschifffahrtsstraßen enthalten. Antwort (b) beschreibt Nachrichten für Seefahrer (NfS/BfS), die aktuelle Änderungen der Seezeichen usw. bekanntgeben, aber keine örtlichen Sondervorschriften darstellen. Antworten (c) und (d) beziehen sich auf sachfremde Veröffentlichungen und Gesetze.
explanation.en: The correct answer is (a): the GDWS Bekanntmachungen are the official local supplementary regulations that add specific rules and guidance for each individual Seeschifffahrtsstraße beyond what SeeSchStrO and EmsSchO cover. Answer (b) describes Notices to Mariners (NfS/BfS), which are navigational update publications, not local special regulations. Answers (c) and (d) refer to unrelated publications and laws that do not constitute local special regulations in this context.
explanation.memoryAid: GDWS = local rules for each German seaway — think 'G' for 'Gebiet' (local area).

en.question: What type of vessel is this and what must be observed?
answers: A public-service vessel on duty. It is permitted to deviate from traffic regulations.
A German Federal Navy vessel on duty. It is carrying ammunition or other dangerous goods on board.
A pilot vessel with special rights on duty. It is permitted to deviate from the keep-to-starboard rule.
A vessel constrained by her draught. She must not be impeded.

explanation.de: Das gezeigte Lichtbild (blaues Funkellicht) kennzeichnet ein Fahrzeug des öffentlichen Dienstes (z. B. Polizei, Zoll, Feuerwehr) im Einsatz gemäß der Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO). Solche Fahrzeuge dürfen im Einsatz von den allgemeinen Verkehrsvorschriften abweichen. Ein tiefgangsbehindertes Fahrzeug oder ein Lotsenfahrzeug würden andere spezifische Lichter führen.
explanation.en: The light signal shown (a blue flashing light) identifies a public-service vessel (e.g. police, customs, fire service) on duty under the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO). Such vessels are permitted to deviate from general traffic regulations while on duty. A vessel constrained by draught or a pilot vessel would display different, specific lights.
explanation.memoryAid: Blue flash = public service dash — they can bend the rules on duty.

en.question: Who gives the visual signal "luminous balls with white stars" and what must be observed?
answers: A vessel of the Bundeswehr (German Armed Forces), the Federal Police, or a power-driven vessel towing shooting targets during exercises. Keep clear.
A vessel fishing with nets, lines, trawls, or other fishing gear, drawing attention to itself. Maintain sufficient distance.
A vessel in distress, drawing attention to itself. Render assistance and, if necessary, request further help.
A power-driven vessel over 50 m in length requesting a pilot. Maintain course and speed.

explanation.de: Leuchtraketen oder Leuchtkugeln mit weißen Sternen werden bei militärischen oder Bundespolizei-Übungen eingesetzt, um darauf hinzuweisen, dass Schießbetrieb stattfindet und Schießscheiben geschleppt werden. Andere Fahrzeuge müssen sich vom Übungsbereich fernhalten. Rote Leuchtsignale (z. B. Fallschirmleuchtraketen) hingegen sind typische Seenotsignale – weiße Sterne bedeuten hier also gerade keine Notlage.
explanation.en: Luminous balls or rockets with white stars are used during Bundeswehr or Federal Police exercises to indicate that live firing is taking place and shooting targets are being towed. Other vessels must keep clear of the exercise area. Red pyrotechnic signals (e.g. parachute flares) are the classic distress signals — white stars therefore do not indicate a vessel in distress.
explanation.memoryAid: White stars = watch out, military at work (not a mayday — mayday flares are red).

en.question: What are fairways (Fahrwasser) within the meaning of the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO) and the Schifffahrtsordnung Emsmündung (EmsSchO)?
answers: They are stretches of water continuously bounded or marked by lateral fairway marks, and — inward of river mouths — also unmarked stretches of water designated for through navigation.
They are stretches of water approved for seagoing vessels; inward of river mouths, inland vessels and pleasure craft are also permitted.
They are stretches of water continuously bounded or marked by lateral fairway marks, on which water-skiing and personal watercraft are permitted provided that through navigation is not impeded.
They are stretches of water continuously bounded or marked by lateral fairway marks, on which the Sportbootführerscheinverordnung (pleasure craft licence regulation) applies.

explanation.de: Laut SeeSchStrO und EmsSchO sind Fahrwasser entweder durch seitliche Betonnung/Befeuerung durchgehend begrenzte Wasserflächen oder — binnenwärts der Flussmündungen — auch nicht besonders gekennzeichnete Wasserflächen, sofern sie dem durchgehenden Schiffsverkehr dienen. Die anderen Antworten erfinden Regelungen (erlaubtes Wasserskifahren, Gültigkeit der Führerscheinverordnung) oder beschränken den Begriff fälschlicherweise auf Seeschiffe.
explanation.en: Under the SeeSchStrO and EmsSchO, fairways are either stretches of water continuously bounded by lateral buoyage/lighting, or — landward of river mouths — also unmarked stretches designated for through shipping traffic. The other options invent rules (permitted water-skiing, applicability of the licence regulation) or incorrectly restrict the definition to seagoing vessels only.
explanation.memoryAid: Fairway = marked channel OR, upriver, any water meant for through traffic.

en.question: Which is — except in tidal flat (Watt) areas — the starboard side of a fairway?
answers: It is the side that a vessel coming from seaward has on its starboard side.
It is the side that a vessel coming from seaward has on its port side.
It is the side marked with red buoys when coming from seaward.
It is the side on which the buoys are marked with consecutive even numbers.

explanation.de: Die Steuerbordseite eines Fahrwassers ist per Definition die Seite, die ein von See einlaufendes Schiff an seiner Steuerbordseite hat. In der IALA-Region A (Europa) wird diese Seite mit grünen Tonnen markiert, nicht mit roten — daher ist Antwort c falsch. Gerade Zahlen kennzeichnen in einigen Systemen die Backbordseite, nicht die Steuerbordseite — daher ist Antwort d falsch.
explanation.en: The starboard side of a fairway is by definition the side that a vessel entering from seaward has on its starboard side. In IALA Region A (Europe), this side is marked with green buoys, not red ones — making answer c incorrect. Even numbers in some buoyage systems mark the port side, not the starboard side — making answer d incorrect.
explanation.memoryAid: Ship coming FROM the sea: starboard side of the channel = your starboard hand.

en.question: What traffic-law obligation does a vessel master have under § 3 of the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO) if the vessel is equipped with a VHF radio installation?
answers: The master is obliged to monitor and take into account the traffic information and traffic assistance provided by the Vessel Traffic Service (VTS).
The master is obliged to hold the appropriate radio certificate when operating a VHF radio installation.
The master is obliged, in conditions of reduced visibility, to regularly report the vessel's name and position to the Vessel Traffic Service.
The master is obliged to keep the radio installation in operation while underway and to record all messages concerning the vessel in the ship's logbook.

explanation.de: Nach § 3 SeeSchStrO muss ein Fahrzeugführer, dessen Schiff mit einer UKW-Funkanlage ausgerüstet ist, die Verkehrsinformationen und -unterstützungen der zuständigen Verkehrszentrale abhören und bei seiner Fahrt berücksichtigen. Dies dient der Sicherheit und Ordnung des Schiffsverkehrs auf den Seeschifffahrtsstraßen. Die anderen Antworten beschreiben zwar grundsätzlich sinnvolle Pflichten, entsprechen aber nicht dem spezifischen Regelungsinhalt des § 3 SeeSchStrO.
explanation.en: Under § 3 SeeSchStrO, a vessel master whose vessel is equipped with a VHF radio installation is specifically required to monitor and take into account the traffic information and assistance broadcast by the competent Vessel Traffic Service (VTS). This ensures safe and orderly navigation on German coastal waterways. The other options may reflect general good practice or other regulations, but they do not capture the specific legal obligation stated in § 3 SeeSchStrO.
explanation.memoryAid: VHF fitted = VTS listened: if you have the radio, you must monitor the traffic centre.

en.question: What light must a sailing vessel of less than 12 m in length, or a vessel under oars, display on the Seeschifffahrtsstraße (German coastal waterway) if it cannot exhibit the lights prescribed by the Collision Regulations (COLREGs)?
answers: An all-round white light.
An all-round red light.
A white masthead light.
A tricolour lantern.

explanation.de: Wenn ein Segelfahrzeug unter 12 m oder ein Ruderfahrzeug die nach KVR vorgeschriebenen Lichter nicht führen kann, genügt ein weißes Rundumlicht als Mindestanforderung, damit das Fahrzeug für andere sichtbar ist. Ein Topplicht (Antwort c) ist kein Rundumlicht und wäre daher nicht ausreichend; eine Dreifarbenlaterne (Antwort d) ist nur für Segelfahrzeuge unter 20 m zulässig, wenn die normale Lichterführung möglich ist.
explanation.en: When a sailing vessel under 12 m or a vessel under oars cannot exhibit the lights required by the COLREGs, a single all-round white light is the minimum requirement to make the vessel visible to others. A masthead light (option c) is not all-round and would be insufficient; a tricolour lantern (option d) is only permitted for sailing vessels under 20 m when proper navigation lights can be carried.
explanation.memoryAid: Small sail, no full lights? One white light shining all around keeps you seen.

en.question: When may a power-driven vessel of less than 7 m in length not navigate on Seeschifffahrtsstraßen (German coastal waterways) if it is unable to exhibit the lights prescribed by the Collision Regulations (COLREGs)?
answers: It may not navigate during the period when the display of lights is prescribed, unless a state of emergency exists.
It may not navigate during the period between sunrise and sunset.
It may only navigate during the period when the display of lights is prescribed if an operationally required signal horn is on board.
It may not navigate during the period between sunset and sunrise.

explanation.de: Fahrzeuge, die die vorgeschriebenen Lichter nicht führen können, dürfen grundsätzlich nicht in der Zeit fahren, in der Lichterführung vorgeschrieben ist (also bei eingeschränkter Sicht und von Sonnenuntergang bis Sonnenaufgang). Eine Ausnahme gilt nur bei einem Notstand. Antwort d) ist unvollständig, da die Lichterführungspflicht nicht nur nachts, sondern auch bei verminderter Sicht tagsüber gelten kann.
explanation.en: Vessels that cannot exhibit the prescribed lights are generally prohibited from navigating during the period when lights are required (i.e. from sunset to sunrise and in restricted visibility). The only exception is a state of emergency. Answer d) is incomplete because the obligation to show lights can apply not only at night but also during the day in restricted visibility.
explanation.memoryAid: No lights = no go — unless emergency makes it so.

en.question: Which sound signal must be given when entering a fairway or harbour if the traffic situation requires it?
answers: One prolonged blast.
One short blast.
One short blast followed by one prolonged blast.
One prolonged blast followed by one short blast.

explanation.de: Beim Einlaufen in ein Fahrwasser oder einen Hafen ist, wenn es die Verkehrslage erfordert, ein langer Ton zu geben. Dieses Signal dient dazu, auf das eigene Manöver aufmerksam zu machen und entgegenkommende oder ausfahrende Fahrzeuge zu warnen. Die anderen Signalkombinationen haben andere Bedeutungen (z. B. ein kurzer Ton = Ich ändere meinen Kurs nach Steuerbord).
explanation.en: When entering a fairway or harbour, one prolonged blast must be given if the traffic situation requires it. This signal alerts other vessels to the manoeuvre and warns any outbound or crossing traffic. The other combinations have different meanings — for example, one short blast means 'I am altering my course to starboard'.
explanation.memoryAid: Think of a prolonged blast as a long 'announcement': you are arriving and making your presence known.

en.question: What is the meaning of the following sound signal?
answers: General danger and warning signal.
Closure of the sea waterway (Seeschifffahrtsstraße).
Stop immediately (public service vessel).
Bridge/lock cannot be opened temporarily.

explanation.de: Das allgemeine Gefahr- und Warnsignal besteht aus mindestens fünf kurzen Tönen und bedeutet, dass eine unmittelbare Gefahr besteht oder eine Warnung ausgegeben wird. Die anderen Optionen beschreiben Signale mit anderem Rhythmus oder anderen Zwecken.
explanation.en: The general danger and warning signal consists of at least five short blasts, indicating an immediate danger or issuing a warning to other vessels. The other options describe signals with different rhythms or purposes and do not apply to this sound pattern.
explanation.memoryAid: Five or more short blasts = DANGER — think 'rapid honking = panic'.

en.question: What is the "general danger and warning signal"?
answers: Two groups of one long and four short blasts each.
Two groups of three long blasts each.
Two groups of four short blasts each.
Two groups of one short and four long blasts each.

explanation.de: Das allgemeine Gefahr- und Warnsignal besteht aus zwei Gruppen von je einem langen und vier kurzen Tönen. Dieses Signal wird z. B. in der Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO) verwendet, um andere Verkehrsteilnehmer auf eine Gefahr aufmerksam zu machen. Die anderen Antworten beschreiben falsche Tonfolgen.
explanation.en: The general danger and warning signal consists of two groups of one long blast followed by four short blasts each. This signal is used (e.g. under the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung) to alert other traffic to a hazard. The other options describe incorrect blast sequences.
explanation.memoryAid: 1 long + 4 short = 'DANGER!' — the long blast leads, four short blasts urgently follow, repeated twice.

en.question: When must the "general danger and warning signal" be given?
answers: When a vessel is endangering another vessel or is itself being endangered by another vessel.
When a vessel intends to overtake another vessel in the fairway on the starboard side.
When a vessel is unable to give way to another vessel.
When a vessel is calling upon another vessel for assistance.

explanation.de: Das allgemeine Gefahr- und Warnsignal (fünf oder mehr kurze Töne) wird gegeben, wenn ein Fahrzeug ein anderes gefährdet oder selbst durch ein anderes gefährdet wird — es ist ein gegenseitiger Warnhinweis auf eine gefährliche Situation. Überholsignale, Manövrierfähigkeit und Hilferuf-Signale sind eigenständige Signale mit eigenen Regelungen.
explanation.en: The general danger and warning signal (five or more short blasts on the whistle) is given whenever one vessel is endangering or is being endangered by another — it is a mutual alert that a dangerous situation exists. Overtaking signals, inability to manoeuvre, and distress/assistance calls are separate, specific signals governed by their own rules.
explanation.memoryAid: Five short blasts = danger exists — either you're the threat or you're threatened.

en.question: How must vessels behave when entering a fairway, crossing a fairway, turning within a fairway, or leaving their anchorage or berth?
answers: They must give way to vessels following the course of the fairway.
They have right of way over vessels already in the fairway.
They must sound one short blast as an attention signal.
They must carry out their manoeuvre in such a way that other vessels are not impeded.

explanation.de: Fahrzeuge, die in ein Fahrwasser einlaufen, es queren, darin drehen oder Anker- bzw. Liegeplätze verlassen, müssen die Vorfahrt der Fahrzeuge beachten, die dem Fahrwasserverlauf folgen. Das bedeutet, dass die im Fahrwasser fahrenden Fahrzeuge Vorfahrt haben – nicht umgekehrt (Antwort b ist falsch). Ein einzelnes Achtungssignal (Antwort c) allein reicht nicht aus und ersetzt nicht die Wartepflicht.
explanation.en: Vessels entering, crossing, turning in a fairway, or leaving a berth/anchorage must give way to vessels already navigating along the fairway. The vessels following the fairway have right of way — not the vessel joining or crossing (answer b is wrong). Sounding one short blast (answer c) alone is insufficient and does not substitute for the obligation to yield.
explanation.memoryAid: Think: the fairway is like a main road — traffic already on it has priority over those joining or crossing.

en.question: How must sailing vessels in a fairway that are not clearly following the direction of the fairway give way to one another?
answers: They must give way to one another in accordance with the rules of the COLREGs, provided they do not thereby endanger or impede vessels with right of way.

They must give way to one another in accordance with the rules of the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (German Coastal Waterways Regulations), provided they do not thereby endanger or impede vessels with right of way.

They must give way to one another in accordance with the rules of the Schifffahrtsordnung Emsmündung (Ems Estuary Navigation Order), provided they do not thereby endanger or impede vessels with right of way.

They must give way to one another in accordance with the rules of the Binnenschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (Inland Waterways Regulations), provided they do not thereby endanger or impede vessels with right of way.

explanation.de: Segelfahrzeuge im Fahrwasser, die nicht deutlich der Fahrwasserrichtung folgen, gelten als außerhalb des Fahrwassers navigierend und unterliegen daher den allgemeinen Ausweichregeln der KVR (Kollisionsverhütungsregeln). Die Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung, die Schifffahrtsordnung Emsmündung und die Binnenschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung gelten in diesem Kontext nicht.
explanation.en: Sailing vessels in a fairway that are not clearly following the fairway's direction are treated as navigating outside the fairway and are therefore subject to the general collision-avoidance rules of the COLREGs. The other regulations listed (Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung, Schifffahrtsordnung Emsmündung, Binnenschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung) do not apply in this context.
explanation.memoryAid: Not following the fairway = back to COLREG basics.

en.question: Which collision avoidance rules apply outside the fairway?
answers: The rules of the COLREGs.
The rules of the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (German Coastal Waters Navigation Order).
The rules of the Schifffahrtsordnung Emsmündung (Ems Estuary Navigation Order).
The rules of the Binnenschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (Inland Waterways Navigation Order).

explanation.de: Außerhalb des Fahrwassers gelten die internationalen Kollisionsverhütungsregeln (KVR/COLREGs), da dort keine speziellen nationalen Sonderregelungen wie die SeeSchStrO greifen. Die SeeSchStrO und ähnliche Verordnungen gelten nur innerhalb bestimmter Fahrwasser und Küstengewässer. Die BinSchStrO betrifft ausschließlich Binnengewässer.
explanation.en: Outside the fairway, the international COLREGs apply, as no special national regulations such as the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung are in force there. The Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung and similar orders only apply within specific defined fairways and coastal waters. The Binnenschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung applies exclusively to inland waterways.
explanation.memoryAid: Open water = open COLREGs: beyond the fairway, international rules take over.

en.question: Where is overtaking prohibited?
answers: At narrows, blind bends, in lock areas, within sections marked by overtaking-prohibition signs, and in the vicinity of non-freely-navigating ferries underway.
At narrows, blind bends, in lock areas, within sections marked by overtaking-prohibition signs, in the vicinity of non-freely-navigating ferries underway, and outside the fairway.
At narrows, blind bends, in lock areas, within sections marked by overtaking-prohibition signs, in the vicinity of non-freely-navigating ferries underway, and in traffic separation schemes.
At narrows, blind bends, within sections marked by overtaking-prohibition signs, and in national parks and specially designated nature reserves.

explanation.de: Nach der Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO) ist das Überholen an Engstellen, unübersichtlichen Krümmungen, in Schleusenbereichen, innerhalb durch Überholverbotszeichen gekennzeichneter Strecken sowie in der Nähe nicht frei fahrender Fähren verboten. Die Antworten b und c fügen Bedingungen (außerhalb des Fahrwassers bzw. Verkehrstrennungsgebiete) hinzu, die nicht zu dieser Regelung gehören, und Antwort d lässt Schleusenbereiche und Fähren weg.
explanation.en: Under the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO), overtaking is prohibited at narrows, blind bends, in lock areas, within sections marked by overtaking-prohibition signs, and near non-freely-navigating ferries underway. Options b and c add conditions (outside the fairway and traffic separation schemes respectively) that do not belong to this rule, while option d omits lock areas and ferries.
explanation.memoryAid: NOBLE Ferries: Narrows, blOck (locks), Blind bends, markEd zones, non-freely-navigating Ferries — the five forbidden zones.

en.question: Where is it permitted to water-ski, ride a personal watercraft (jet ski), or sail a windsurfboard?
answers: Outside the fairway, unless prohibited by the General Directorate for Waterways and Shipping (GDWS) by official notice. Within the fairway on sections that have been announced by the GDWS or are marked by blue signs bearing the white symbol of a water-skier, a personal watercraft, or a windsurfer.

Outside the sea waterway (Seeschifffahrtsstraße), unless prohibited by the General Directorate for Waterways and Shipping (GDWS) by official notice. Within the sea waterway on sections that have been announced by the GDWS or are marked by blue signs bearing the white symbol of a water-skier, a personal watercraft, or a windsurfer.
On the high seas and on waters connected thereto that are navigable by seagoing vessels, provided a minimum distance of 100 m from the shore is maintained.

Within the fairway, unless prohibited by the General Directorate for Waterways and Shipping (GDWS) by official notice. Outside the fairway on sections that have been announced by the GDWS or are marked by blue signs bearing the white symbol of a water-skier, a personal watercraft, or a windsurfer.

explanation.de: Die Grundregel lautet: Wasserski, Wassermotorrad und Segelsurfen sind außerhalb des Fahrwassers erlaubt, sofern keine behördliche Verbotsbekanntmachung der GDWS vorliegt. Im Fahrwasser selbst ist es nur auf eigens ausgewiesenen Abschnitten – per Bekanntmachung oder durch die charakteristischen blauen Schilder mit weißem Symbol – gestattet. Antwort b verwechselt 'Fahrwasser' mit 'Seeschifffahrtsstraße', und Antwort d dreht die Regel genau um.
explanation.en: The basic rule is: water-skiing, personal watercraft, and windsurfing are permitted outside the fairway, as long as the GDWS has not issued a prohibiting notice. Within the fairway, these activities are only allowed on specially designated sections – announced by the GDWS or marked by the characteristic blue signs with a white symbol. Answer b incorrectly substitutes 'Seeschifffahrtsstraße' (sea waterway) for 'Fahrwasser' (fairway), and answer d reverses the rule entirely.
explanation.memoryAid: Outside the fairway = free to go (unless banned); inside the fairway = only where the blue sign says so.

en.question: How must the operators of tow boats for water-skiers, personal watercraft riders, and windsurfers behave when approaching other vessels?
answers: They must give way.
When approaching other vessels, they must stop and avoid suction and wash.
They have right of way and must cross ahead of the other vessel's bow.
They must maintain their course and speed.

explanation.de: Nach den deutschen Schifffahrtsregeln müssen Zugboote für Wasserskiläufer, Wassermotorradfahrer und Segelsurfer beim Annähern an andere Fahrzeuge ausweichen. Sie haben weder Vorfahrt noch dürfen sie Kurs und Geschwindigkeit beibehalten. Das bloße Aufstoppengebot gilt für andere Fahrzeugkategorien in bestimmten Situationen, nicht für diesen Fall.
explanation.en: Under German inland and coastal waterway regulations, tow boats engaged in towing water-skiers, personal watercraft, or windsurfers are considered stand-on vessels with reduced maneuverability — but in practice, they are required to give way to all other vessels when approaching them. Options B–D are incorrect: stopping is not the prescribed behaviour, they do not have right of way, and they may not simply maintain course and speed.
explanation.memoryAid: Tow boats always yield — the skier behind you doesn't give you priority.

en.question: Where is anchoring prohibited?
answers: In the fairway, at narrow passages and in curves with restricted visibility; within 300 m of floating equipment, wrecks and other navigational obstructions, cable buoys and other locations used for military and civilian purposes; in front of harbour entrances, locks, landing stages and sluices, and in the approach channels of the Kiel Canal (Nord-Ostsee-Kanal); within ferry and bridge sections; 300 m before and after no-anchoring signs.

In the fairway, on Seeschifffahrtsstraßen (federally designated sea waterways), at narrow passages and in curves with restricted visibility; within 300 m of floating equipment, wrecks and other navigational obstructions, cable buoys and other locations used for military and civilian purposes; in front of harbour entrances, locks, landing stages and sluices, and in the approach channels of the Kiel Canal; within ferry and bridge sections; 300 m before and after no-anchoring signs.

In the fairway, at narrow passages and in curves with restricted visibility; within 300 m of floating equipment, cable buoys and other locations used for military and civilian purposes; in front of harbour entrances, locks, landing stages and sluices, and in the approach channels of the Kiel Canal, and in bird and nature reserves as well as generally within national parks.
In the fairway, when it has been announced by the Generaldirektion Wasserstraßen und Schifffahrt (GDWS). Outside the fairway on sections announced by the GDWS or marked by corresponding visual signs.

explanation.de: Die korrekte Antwort (a) listet die nach der Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO) geltenden Ankerverbotsbereiche vollständig und korrekt auf. Antwort (b) ist falsch, weil sie zusätzlich 'auf Seeschifffahrtsstraßen' als eigenständige Kategorie nennt, was so nicht in der Regel steht. Antwort (c) fehlt die Nennung von Wracks und sonstigen Schifffahrtshindernissen und fügt stattdessen Schutzgebiete hinzu, die nicht pauschal als Ankerverbotszonen gelten.
explanation.en: The correct answer (a) completely and accurately lists the anchoring prohibition zones as defined by the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO). Answer (b) is incorrect because it adds 'on Seeschifffahrtsstraßen' as a separate standalone category, which does not appear in the regulation. Answer (c) omits wrecks and other navigational obstructions and instead incorrectly adds nature/bird reserves and national parks as blanket anchoring prohibitions.
explanation.memoryAid: Think '300 m rule': fairways, narrows, blind bends, wrecks, cables, harbour entrances, locks, ferry/bridge stretches — all off-limits, plus 300 m either side of a no-anchor sign.

en.question: What must be done to warn other vessels when your own boat has sunk and represents a navigational hazard?
answers: You notify the maritime police authority (Schifffahrtspolizeibehörde) and provide the position if possible.
You notify the Deutsche Gesellschaft zur Rettung Schiffbrüchiger (German Maritime Search and Rescue Society) so that the hazard can be marked.
You transmit a distress signal.
You notify the Bundesamt für Seeschifffahrt und Hydrographie (Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency) and provide the position if possible.

explanation.de: Wenn ein gesunkenes Fahrzeug ein Schifffahrtshindernis darstellt, ist die zuständige Schifffahrtspolizeibehörde zu informieren und möglichst die genaue Position anzugeben, damit sie Warnmaßnahmen für die Schifffahrt einleiten kann. Die DGzRS ist für Seenotrettung zuständig, nicht für das Markieren von Hindernissen; das BSH ist eine Fachbehörde, aber nicht die zuständige Stelle für solche Meldungen.
explanation.en: When a sunken vessel constitutes a navigational hazard, the competent maritime police authority must be informed with the position if known, so that it can initiate appropriate warnings for other traffic. The DGzRS handles search and rescue, not the marking of obstructions; the BSH is a technical agency but not the responsible authority for such reports.
explanation.memoryAid: Sunken = Police report: the maritime police authority manages navigational hazard warnings.

en.question: Under which signal are pleasure craft permitted to enter the locks of the Kiel Canal (Nord-Ostsee-Kanal)?
answers: When a white interrupted light is shown.
When a white flashing light is shown.
When two green lights side by side are shown.
When a single green occulting light is shown.

explanation.de: Im Nord-Ostsee-Kanal dürfen Sportfahrzeuge in eine Schleuse einfahren, wenn ein weißes unterbrochenes Licht gezeigt wird. Die anderen genannten Lichtsignale gelten für andere Fahrzeugkategorien oder haben eine abweichende Bedeutung und erlauben Sportfahrzeugen keine Einfahrt.
explanation.en: On the Kiel Canal (Nord-Ostsee-Kanal), pleasure craft are permitted to enter a lock when a white interrupted light (weißes unterbrochenes Licht) is displayed. The other light signals (white flashing, two green side by side, green occulting) indicate different instructions or apply to other vessel categories, and do not authorise pleasure craft entry.
explanation.memoryAid: White interrupted = Welcome in — the broken white light gives pleasure craft the go-ahead at NOK locks.

en.question: Where can the rules for transiting the Kiel Canal (Nord-Ostsee-Kanal, NOK) be found?
answers: Supplementary regulations for the NOK in the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (German Seaways Regulations) and in the notices of the Generaldirektion Wasserstraßen und Schifffahrt (GDWS).
Supplementary regulations for the NOK in the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung and in the Collision Regulations (COLREGs).
Supplementary regulations for the NOK in the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung and in the Sportbootführerscheinverordnung (Recreational Craft Licence Ordinance).
Supplementary regulations for the NOK in the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung and in the Seeaufgabengesetz (Maritime Functions Act).

explanation.de: Die Vorschriften für die Durchfahrt durch den Nord-Ostsee-Kanal (NOK) sind in den Ergänzenden Vorschriften der Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO) sowie in den aktuellen Bekanntmachungen der Generaldirektion Wasserstraßen und Schifffahrt (GDWS) geregelt. Die Kollisionsverhütungsregeln, die Sportbootführerscheinverordnung und das Seeaufgabengesetz enthalten keine spezifischen NOK-Durchfahrtsvorschriften.
explanation.en: The rules for transiting the Kiel Canal (NOK) are found in the supplementary regulations of the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung (SeeSchStrO) together with the current notices issued by the Generaldirektion Wasserstraßen und Schifffahrt (GDWS). The COLREGs, the Recreational Craft Licence Ordinance, and the Maritime Functions Act do not contain specific NOK transit regulations.
explanation.memoryAid: GDWS issues the notices that keep NOK rules up to date — always check both the SeeSchStrO and the GDWS announcements.

en.question: What do three flashing red lights displayed one above the other on a junction signal mast in the Kiel Canal (Nord-Ostsee-Kanal) signify, and what must be observed?
answers: Departure prohibited for all vessels; wait for the signal to be cancelled.
Sensitive installation; reduce speed, avoid suction and wash.
Permanent closure of the waterway; proceeding further is prohibited.
Permanent closure of a section of the waterway; proceeding further in that section is prohibited.

explanation.de: Drei unterbrochene (blinkende) rote Lichter übereinander an einem Weichensignalmast im Nord-Ostsee-Kanal bedeuten, dass das Ausfahren aus der betreffenden Weiche (Ausweichstelle) für alle Fahrzeuge verboten ist. Fahrzeuge müssen warten, bis das Signal aufgehoben wird. Drei Dauerlichter hingegen würden eine dauerhafte Sperrung anzeigen – die Unterbrechung (Blinken) kennzeichnet das temporäre Ausfahrverbot.
explanation.en: Three interrupted (flashing) red lights displayed vertically on a junction signal mast in the Kiel Canal indicate that departure from the passing bay (Weiche) is prohibited for all vessels. Vessels must wait until the signal is cancelled. Steady (non-flashing) red lights would indicate a permanent closure — the flashing character specifically marks this as a temporary prohibition on leaving the bay.
explanation.memoryAid: Flashing red = wait in the bay instead — three blinks mean 'don't exit yet'.

en.question: What is the meaning of the following board sign?
answers: The speed through the water in km/h — on the Nord-Ostsee-Kanal (NOK) the speed over ground in km/h — that must not be exceeded.
The minimum distance in metres that must be maintained from the location of the sign along the subsequent stretch.
The speed through the water in nautical miles per hour (knots) — on the Nord-Ostsee-Kanal (NOK) the speed over ground in nautical miles per hour — that must not be exceeded.
The minimum distance to other vessels in metres that must not be undercut in the announced stretch of waterway.

explanation.de: Auf den deutschen Seeschifffahrtsstraßen geben Geschwindigkeitstafeln die zulässige Höchstgeschwindigkeit in km/h durchs Wasser an; auf dem Nord-Ostsee-Kanal gilt sie als Geschwindigkeit über Grund. Antwort (c) ist falsch, weil die Einheit km/h und nicht Knoten ist; Antworten (b) und (d) beschreiben Abstandstafeln, keine Geschwindigkeitstafeln.
explanation.en: On German inland and coastal waterways (governed by the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung), speed limit signs show the maximum permitted speed in km/h through the water; the NOK is an exception where the limit applies over ground. Answer (c) is wrong because the unit is km/h, not knots; answers (b) and (d) describe distance signs, not speed signs.
explanation.memoryAid: km/h on the sign = km/h through the water (NOK: over ground) — always kilometres, never knots.

en.question: What is the meaning of the following visual signals?
answers: Installation requiring protection.
Permanent closure of a section of the sea waterway (Seeschifffahrtsstraße).
Permanent closure of the sea waterway (Seeschifffahrtsstraße).
Extraordinary obstruction to navigation.

explanation.de: Das angezeigte Sichtzeichen kennzeichnet eine schutzbedürftige Anlage (z. B. Unterwasserkabel oder -leitungen), die besonderer Vorsicht bedarf. Die anderen Antworten beschreiben Sperrungen oder Behinderungen, die durch andere, spezifische Sichtzeichen angezeigt werden.
explanation.en: The visual signal shown marks an installation requiring protection (e.g. underwater cables or pipelines), indicating that special caution is needed in the vicinity. The other answer options describe closures or obstructions, which are indicated by different, specific visual signals under the Seeschifffahrtsstraßen-Ordnung.

en.question: What is the meaning of the following sound signal and what must be observed?
answers: Bridge, barrage, or lock cannot be opened temporarily; stop and wait for clearance.
A vessel required to give way is being reminded of its obligation by the stand-on vessel; initiate a give-way manoeuvre immediately.
Keep-away signal, danger due to hazardous cargo; leave the danger area immediately. Avoid open flames (risk of explosion).
Bridge, barrage, or lock is being prepared for opening; continue passage.

explanation.de: Das Signal bedeutet, dass eine Brücke, ein Sperrwerk oder eine Schleuse vorübergehend nicht geöffnet werden kann. Fahrzeuge müssen anhalten und auf die Freigabe warten. Option d ist falsch, weil dieses Signal keine bevorstehende Öffnung ankündigt, sondern eine Sperrung anzeigt.
explanation.en: This sound signal indicates that a bridge, barrage, or lock cannot be opened temporarily. Vessels must stop and await clearance before proceeding. Option d is incorrect because this signal does not announce an imminent opening — it signals that passage is currently blocked.
explanation.memoryAid: Cannot open = Stop and wait; not 'coming soon — carry on'.

en.question: What is the meaning of the following visual sign?
answers: Speed of 8 km/h through the water, which must not be exceeded within an area of 500 m from the respective shoreline due to bathing activity.
