explanation.de: Der Koppelort wird rechnerisch und zeichnerisch ermittelt, indem man von einem bekannten Ausgangspunkt aus die gesteuerten Kurse und zurückgelegten Distanzen sowie alle vorhersehbaren Einflüsse wie Strom und Abtrift berücksichtigt. Antwort (b) und (c) beschreiben Kreuzpeilungen bzw. Standlinienverfahren, bei denen keine Vorausberechnung aus einem früheren Standort erfolgt. Antwort (d) ist unvollständig, da die vorhersehbaren Einflüsse fehlen.
explanation.en: A dead reckoning position (Koppelort) is found mathematically and graphically by advancing from a known position using the courses steered and distances run, while also accounting for all foreseeable external influences such as current and leeway. Answer (b) describes a cross-bearing fix, and answer (c) describes a standard two-bearing fix — neither involves reckoning from prior position data. Answer (d) is a partial description that omits the key element of accounting for foreseeable external influences.
explanation.memoryAid: Dead reckoning = Dead certainty from Courses + Distances + Current — no landmarks needed.

en.question: What must be observed when installing a magnetic compass on board?
answers: The lubber line must run parallel to the keel line. The compass must be easily readable and must not be installed near iron parts.
The compass must run parallel to the keel line. The compass must be easily readable and must not be installed near iron parts.
The lubber line must run parallel to the keel line. The compass must have easily readable figures and must not be installed near iron parts.
The compass must run parallel to the keel line. The compass must have easily readable figures and must not be installed near iron parts.

explanation.de: Richtig ist (a): Es ist der Steuerstrich – nicht das Kompassgehäuse selbst –, der parallel zur Kiellinie ausgerichtet sein muss, damit der Kompass den tatsächlichen Schiffskurs anzeigt. Außerdem muss der Kompass insgesamt gut ablesbar sein und darf nicht in der Nähe von Eisenteilen aufgestellt werden, da diese eine Deviation verursachen würden. Antworten (b) und (d) nennen fälschlicherweise den Kompass (statt den Steuerstrich) als das auszurichtende Element, während (c) und (d) 'gut ablesbar' zu eng auf 'gut ablesbare Zahlen' einschränken.
explanation.en: The correct answer is (a): it is the lubber line (Steuerstrich) — not the compass housing itself — that must be aligned parallel to the keel, so that the compass accurately indicates the vessel's heading. The compass must also be generally easy to read (not just have readable figures) and must be kept away from ferrous materials that could cause deviation. Options (b) and (d) incorrectly say the compass (housing) must be parallel, and options (c) and (d) incorrectly narrow 'easily readable' to just 'easily readable figures'.
explanation.memoryAid: The LUBBER LINE steers — it must align with the keel, not the compass body.

en.question: What is meant by 'Ebbe' (ebb)?
answers: The falling of the water from high water to the following low water.
The period of time from high water to the following low water.
The lowest water level of a tide.
The difference between high water and low water.

explanation.de: Ebbe bezeichnet den Vorgang des sinkenden Wasserstands vom Hochwasser bis zum nächsten Niedrigwasser. Option B beschreibt zwar denselben Zeitraum, betont aber nicht den Bewegungsvorgang des fallenden Wassers. Option C beschreibt das Niedrigwasser, Option D den Tidenhub.
explanation.en: Ebbe (ebb) specifically refers to the process of the water level falling — i.e. the movement of water from high water (Hochwasser) down to the next low water (Niedrigwasser). Option B describes the same time period but misses the key point that Ebbe is the falling motion itself, not merely a time span. Option C describes Niedrigwasser (low water), and Option D describes Tidenhub (tidal range).
explanation.memoryAid: Ebb = water going Away (falling away from high water).

en.question: What is meant by 'Flut' (flood tide)?
answers: The rising of the water from low water to the following high water.
The period of time from low water to the following high water.
The highest water level of a tidal cycle.
The difference between high water and low water.

explanation.de: Flut bezeichnet den Vorgang des steigenden Wassers – also den Prozess selbst, nicht den Zeitraum. Der Zeitraum heißt 'Flutzeit' oder 'Flutdauer' (Antwort b). Der höchste Wasserstand ist das 'Hochwasser' (Antwort c), und die Differenz zwischen Hoch- und Niedrigwasser nennt man 'Tidenhub' (Antwort d).
explanation.en: Flut (flood tide) refers to the process of water rising from low water to the following high water — it describes the rising movement itself, not the time period. The time period is called 'Flutdauer' (answer b). The highest water level is 'Hochwasser' (high water, answer c), and the difference between high and low water is the 'Tidenhub' (tidal range, answer d).
explanation.memoryAid: Flut = Flow up — the flood tide is the upward flow of water.

en.question: What is meant by a 'Tide' (tidal cycle)?
answers: The period between one low water and the next following low water.
The period between one high water and the next following low water.
The period between one high water and the next following high water.
The period between one low water and the next following high water.

explanation.de: Eine Tide bezeichnet den vollständigen Zeitraum von einem Niedrigwasser bis zum nächsten Niedrigwasser, also einen kompletten Anstieg und Abfall des Wasserstandes (ca. 12 Std. 25 Min.). Optionen b und d beschreiben nur eine halbe Tide, und Option c zählt zwar auch einen vollen Zyklus, beginnt jedoch am Hochwasser statt am Niedrigwasser.
explanation.en: A 'Tide' (tidal cycle) is defined as the full period from one low water to the next low water, encompassing one complete rise and fall — approximately 12 hours 25 minutes. Options b and d only describe half a cycle, and option c, while also a full cycle, starts from high water rather than the conventional low-water reference point.
explanation.memoryAid: A Tide = Low to Low — the full ride.

en.question: What is meant by low water?
answers: The occurrence of the lowest water level at the transition from falling to rising.
The falling of the water after the highest water level has been reached.
The occurrence of the highest water level at the transition from rising to falling.
The rising of the water after the lowest water level has been reached.

explanation.de: Niedrigwasser bezeichnet den Moment, in dem der Wasserstand seinen tiefsten Punkt erreicht – also genau den Übergang vom Fallen zum Steigen der Tide. Es ist ein Zeitpunkt, keine Phase. Antwort b beschreibt das Fallen des Wassers (Ebbe), Antwort c beschreibt das Hochwasser, Antwort d beschreibt das Steigen (Flut).
explanation.en: Low water (Niedrigwasser) is the instant at which the tidal water level reaches its lowest point — the exact transition from the ebbing (falling) phase to the flooding (rising) phase. It is a moment in time, not a process. Option b describes the ebbing phase, option c describes high water, and option d describes the flooding phase.
explanation.memoryAid: Low water = the bottom of the tide curve — the single instant it stops falling and starts rising.

en.question: What is meant by high water (Hochwasser)?
answers: The occurrence of the highest water level at the transition from rising to falling.
The rise of the water after the lowest water level has been reached.
The occurrence of the lowest water level at the transition from falling to rising.
The fall of the water after the highest water level has been reached.

explanation.de: Hochwasser (auch Flut-Hochwasser oder Tidehochwasser) bezeichnet den Moment, in dem der Wasserstand seinen höchsten Punkt erreicht – also den Übergang vom Steigen (Flut) zum Fallen (Ebbe). Antwort c beschreibt das Gegenteil, nämlich Niedrigwasser; Antwort b beschreibt den Vorgang des Steigens selbst (Flut); Antwort d beschreibt das Fallen nach dem Höchststand (Ebbe).
explanation.en: High water (Hochwasser) is the moment when the tidal water level reaches its maximum — the transition point from rising tide (flood) to falling tide (ebb). Answer c describes the opposite: low water (Niedrigwasser). Answer b describes the process of rising water (the flood phase itself), and answer d describes the ebbing phase after high water.
explanation.memoryAid: High water = the PEAK, not the process — it's the turning point at the TOP.

en.question: What is meant by 'tidal range' (Tidenhub)?
answers: The difference in height between high water and low water.
The difference in height between two successive high waters.
The period of time between a low water and the next following high water.
The period of time between a low water and the next following low water.

explanation.de: Der Tidenhub bezeichnet den vertikalen Höhenunterschied zwischen Hochwasser und Niedrigwasser. Antwort b vergleicht zwei aufeinanderfolgende Hochwasser statt Hoch- und Niedrigwasser. Die Antworten c und d beschreiben Zeitspannen (Flutdauer bzw. Tidenperiode), keine Höhenunterschiede.
explanation.en: Tidal range (Tidenhub) is defined as the vertical difference in water level between high tide and low tide. Options b is wrong because it compares two high waters rather than a high and a low. Options c and d describe time intervals (the flood period and tidal cycle respectively), not height differences.
explanation.memoryAid: Hub = Height difference: High minus Low.

en.question: Where can information on high and low water times and the tidal range for a specific location be found?
answers: In the tide tables (Gezeitentafeln) or the tidal calendar (Gezeitenkalender) published by the Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency (BSH).
In the flood forecast (Flutvorhersage) of the Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency (BSH).
In the tidal atlas (Gezeitenatlas) of the Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency (BSH).
In the lunar phase calendar (Mondphasenkalender) of the Federal Institute of Hydrology (BfG).

explanation.de: Gezeitentafeln und Gezeitenkalender des BSH enthalten für konkrete Orte die genauen Zeiten für Hoch- und Niedrigwasser sowie den jeweiligen Tidenhub. Der Gezeitenatlas (Antwort c) zeigt hingegen die Strömungsrichtungen und -stärken zu verschiedenen Tidenphasen, aber keine ortsgebundenen Hoch-/Niedrigwasserzeiten. Ein Mondphasenkalender enthält keine tidenbezogenen Wasserstände.
explanation.en: Tide tables and tidal calendars published by the BSH (Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency) list the precise times of high and low water and the tidal range for specific locations. The tidal atlas (answer c) shows current directions and speeds during tidal phases but does not provide location-specific high/low water times. A lunar phase calendar contains no tidal water level data.
explanation.memoryAid: Tide TIMES and HEIGHTS → Tide TABLES (Gezeitentafeln); atlas = currents, not times.

en.question: How long should a towline be in heavy seas?
answers: At least two to three times the wavelength.
At least two to three times the wave height.
At least two to three times the vessel's length.
At least two to three times the water depth.

explanation.de: Bei starkem Seegang sollte die Schleppleine mindestens zwei- bis dreifache Wellenlänge betragen, damit sich beide Schiffe im gleichen Wellenrhythmus bewegen – möglichst gleichzeitig auf einem Wellenkamm oder im Wellental. So werden gefährliche Ruckkräfte vermieden. Wellenhöhe oder Schiffslänge sind hierfür keine geeigneten Bezugsgrößen.
explanation.en: In heavy seas, the towline should be at least two to three times the wavelength so that both the towing vessel and the towed vessel ride the waves in the same phase — ideally both on a crest or both in a trough simultaneously. This prevents dangerous snatch loads caused by one vessel being lifted while the other is in a trough. Wave height or ship length are not the relevant reference measures for synchronising wave motion.
explanation.memoryAid: Match the waves: length × 2–3 keeps tug and tow in the same rhythm.

en.question: What must be observed when a pleasure craft is to be towed?
answers: The towline must be adjusted to the sea conditions. The towing speed must not exceed the speed that the tow can achieve under its own power in displacement mode. Sudden jerking taut of the towline must be avoided.

The towline must be adjusted to the sea conditions. The towing speed must not exceed the speed that the towing vessel can achieve under its own power in displacement mode. Sudden jerking taut of the towline must be avoided.

The towline must be adjusted to the weather conditions. The towing speed must not exceed the speed that the tow can achieve under its own power in planing mode. Sudden jerking taut of the towline must be avoided.

The towline must be adjusted to the weather conditions. The towing speed must not exceed the speed that the towing vessel can achieve under its own power in planing mode. Sudden jerking taut of the towline must be avoided.

explanation.de: Maßgeblich ist die Verdrängungsgeschwindigkeit des Anhangs (des geschleppten Fahrzeugs), da dieses die strukturelle Grenze setzt – nicht die des schleppenden Fahrzeugs. Der Bezug ist der Seegang (nicht allgemein das Wetter), da die Schleppleinenlänge und -spannung von den Wellenverhältnissen abhängen. Gleitfahrt als Kriterium (Optionen c/d) ist falsch, weil ein geschlepptes Fahrzeug keinen Gleitvorgang ausführen kann.
explanation.en: The limiting factor for towing speed is the displacement hull speed of the tow (the vessel being towed), not that of the towing vessel, since the tow's hull form sets the structural limit. The towline must be adapted to sea conditions (wave state), not merely general weather. Options c and d are wrong because a vessel under tow cannot achieve planing speed.
explanation.memoryAid: Tow speed = TOW's displacement speed — it's the trailer, not the truck, that sets the limit.

en.question: How can a disabled (unsteerable) recreational vessel be kept bow into the wind?
answers: By using a sea anchor or other suitable floating objects.
By repeatedly briefly engaging and disengaging the drive engine.
By deploying a sea anchor or similar floating objects from the stern.
By deploying sea anchors or other suitable floating objects from both bow and stern.

explanation.de: Ein vom Bug ausgebrachter Treibanker erzeugt Widerstand und hält den Bug in den Wind, was für ein manövrierunfähiges Boot die sicherste Lage ist. Ein achteraus ausgebrachter Treibanker (Antwort c) würde das Heck in den Wind drehen, und Treibanker an beiden Enden (Antwort d) würden gegenläufige Kräfte erzeugen, ohne eine zuverlässige Ausrichtung zu gewährleisten.
explanation.en: A sea anchor (drogue) deployed from the bow creates drag that keeps the bow pointed into the wind and waves, which is the safest orientation for a disabled vessel. Deploying it from the stern (answer c) would hold the stern into the wind, and using it at both ends (answer d) would create opposing forces without reliably holding any orientation.
explanation.memoryAid: Bow anchor = Bow into wind: deploy the sea anchor from the front to face the weather head-on.

en.question: Why should speed be reduced in heavy seas?
answers: To avoid damage caused by wave impact (pounding).
To avoid the propeller breaking the surface and to save fuel.
To minimise rolling and pitching motions.
To avoid bringing the vessel's length and wave length into resonance.

explanation.de: Bei starkem Seegang wird die Fahrt in erster Linie vermindert, um Schäden durch Seeschlag (das harte Aufschlagen des Bugs auf die Wellen) zu vermeiden. Die anderen Antworten beschreiben zwar reale Effekte, sind aber nachrangig — die Gefahr von Strukturschäden durch Seeschlag ist der Hauptgrund für die Fahrtreduzierung.
explanation.en: In heavy seas, reducing speed primarily serves to prevent structural damage caused by wave impact (pounding or seeschlag), where the bow slams into oncoming waves with great force. While the other options describe real phenomena, they are secondary concerns — the risk of serious hull damage from pounding is the principal reason to slow down.
explanation.memoryAid: Heavy seas = slow down to stop the bow from **slamming** — hull damage is the primary risk.

en.question: What does the following symbol mean?
answers: Wind from the direction of northwest; strength: Bft. 3; clear sky.
Wind in the direction of northwest; strength: Bft. 3; clear sky.
Current from the direction of northwest; strength: 3 knots; tidal area.
Current in the direction of northwest; strength: 3 knots; tidal area.

explanation.de: In der meteorologischen Notation zeigt der Windpfeil die Richtung an, AUS der der Wind weht, und die Fiederung gibt die Beaufort-Stärke an. Ein leerer Kreis an der Station steht für wolkenlosen Himmel. Antwort (b) ist falsch, weil Windrichtung immer die Herkunftsrichtung angibt, nicht die Richtung, in die der Wind weht.
explanation.en: In meteorological notation, the wind arrow (barb) points in the direction FROM which the wind is blowing, and the number of barb feathers indicates Beaufort force. A clear circle at the station represents a cloudless sky. Answer (b) is wrong because wind direction is always stated as the direction FROM which it comes, not toward which it blows.
explanation.memoryAid: Wind FROM — the arrow feathers trail behind like a flag blown away from the source.

en.question: What information does the Beaufort scale provide?
answers: Wind forces from 0 to 12 and their effects on the sea.
Wind forces from 0 to 12 and their effects on the coast.
The tidal range at the coast at full moon and new moon.
Wave height and wind speed at storm force.

explanation.de: Die Beaufort-Skala beschreibt Windstärken von 0 (Windstille) bis 12 (Orkan) und deren Auswirkungen auf die Seegangsverhältnisse (z. B. Wellenhöhe, Schaumbildung). Antwort b ist falsch, weil die Skala die Auswirkungen auf die See beschreibt, nicht auf die Küste. Antwort d ist unvollständig, da sie nur einen kleinen Ausschnitt der gesamten Skala darstellt.
explanation.en: The Beaufort scale describes wind forces from 0 (calm) to 12 (hurricane) and their effects on sea conditions (e.g., wave height, foam formation). Answer b is incorrect because the scale describes effects on the sea, not the coast. Answer d is incomplete, as it covers only a small portion of the full scale.
explanation.memoryAid: Beaufort = 0–12, describing the SEA state — not the shore, not just storms.

en.question: How are places of equal air pressure represented on a weather chart, and in what unit is air pressure given?
answers: By isobars and in hectopascals.
By isobars and in millipascals.
By isoclines and in hectopascals.
By isoclines and in decipascals.

explanation.de: Linien gleichen Luftdrucks heißen Isobaren. Der Luftdruck wird in der Meteorologie in Hektopascal (hPa) angegeben (früher: Millibar). Isoklinen verbinden Punkte gleicher Neigung, nicht gleichen Drucks.
explanation.en: Lines connecting points of equal air pressure are called isobars. Meteorological pressure is measured in hectopascals (hPa), equivalent to the older unit millibar. Isoclines connect points of equal inclination/slope, not equal pressure — making options c and d incorrect.
explanation.memoryAid: ISOBARs = same BAR (pressure) — measured in HectoPascals (hPa).

en.question: What must be expected when the barometric pressure drops rapidly?
answers: Strong winds or a storm.
Light winds or calm conditions.
An improvement in the weather.
A deterioration in the weather.

explanation.de: Ein rasch fallender Luftdruck ist ein klassisches Warnsignal für ein herannahendes Tiefdruckgebiet, das Starkwind oder Sturm mit sich bringt. Antwort (d) 'Wetterverschlechterung' ist zwar nicht falsch, aber zu ungenau — die spezifische und unmittelbare Folge eines schnellen Druckabfalls ist Starkwind oder Sturm, weshalb (a) die präzisere Antwort ist.
explanation.en: A rapid drop in barometric pressure is a classic warning sign of an approaching low-pressure system, which brings strong winds or even storm conditions. Answer (d) 'deterioration in weather' is partially correct but too vague — the specific and direct consequence of rapidly falling pressure is strong wind or storm, making (a) the most precise answer.
explanation.memoryAid: Pressure drops fast → winds blast past.

en.question: What do the isobars shown on a weather chart represent?
answers: Places of equal atmospheric pressure.
Places of equal wind strength.
Places of equal cloud formation.
Places of equal humidity.

explanation.de: Isobaren sind Linien auf der Wetterkarte, die alle Orte gleichen Luftdrucks (in Hektopascal) miteinander verbinden. Windstärke, Wolkenbildung und Luftfeuchtigkeit werden durch andere Kartensymbole dargestellt.
explanation.en: Isobars are lines on a weather chart connecting all points that share the same atmospheric pressure (measured in hectopascals). They do not depict wind strength, cloud cover, or humidity — those are shown by other chart symbols or separate diagrams.
explanation.memoryAid: 'Iso' = same, 'bar' = pressure (Greek: baros) — isobars = same-pressure lines.

en.question: What does the following diagram show?
answers: A high-pressure system in the Northern Hemisphere, isobars indicating atmospheric pressure in hPa.
A high-pressure system in the Southern Hemisphere, isobars indicating atmospheric pressure in hPa.
A high-pressure system in the Northern Hemisphere, isobars indicating atmospheric pressure in hPa, direction of movement: northwest.
A high-pressure system in the Southern Hemisphere, isobars indicating atmospheric pressure in hPa, direction of movement: southwest.

explanation.de: Die Abbildung zeigt ein Hochdruckgebiet auf der Nordhalbkugel: Der Luftdruck steigt zur Mitte hin an, und die Windumströmung erfolgt im Uhrzeigersinn — typisch für die Nordhalbkugel. Da kein Pfeil für eine Zugrichtung eingezeichnet ist, scheiden die Antworten c und d aus. Antwort b ist falsch, weil auf der Südhalbkugel die Umströmung eines Hochs gegen den Uhrzeigersinn verläuft.
explanation.en: The diagram shows a high-pressure system (Hochdruckgebiet) in the Northern Hemisphere: pressure values increase toward the centre, and the wind circulation flows clockwise (anticyclonic) around the high — which is characteristic of the Northern Hemisphere. No arrow indicating a direction of movement is shown in the image, so answers c and d (which add a 'direction of movement') are incorrect. Answer b is wrong because in the Southern Hemisphere, anticyclonic circulation would be counter-clockwise.
explanation.memoryAid: Northern Hemisphere High = clockwise (like a clock 'winding up' the pressure).

en.question: What does the following illustration show?
answers: Illustration of a low-pressure system in the Northern Hemisphere with warm and cold fronts, isobars indicating air pressure in hPa, warm and cold air flows.
Illustration of a low-pressure system in the Southern Hemisphere with cold and warm fronts, isobars indicating air pressure in hPa, cold and warm air flows.

Illustration of a low-pressure system in the Northern Hemisphere with the cold front ahead of the warm front, air pressure indicated in hPa, warm front to the south, cold front to the north of the centre.
Illustration of a low-pressure system in the Southern Hemisphere with the warm front ahead of the cold front, air pressure indicated in hPa, depiction of cold and warm air flows.

explanation.de: Das Bild zeigt ein klassisches Tiefdruckgebiet der Nordhalbkugel mit zyklonaler (entgegen dem Uhrzeigersinn) Luftzirkulation, einer voraneilenden Warmfront und einer nachfolgenden Kaltfront sowie Isobaren in hPa. Auf der Südhalbkugel wäre die Zirkulation umgekehrt (im Uhrzeigersinn), was Antworten b und d ausschließt. Antwort c vertauscht die Frontenposition.
explanation.en: The image shows a classic Northern Hemisphere low-pressure system with cyclonic (counter-clockwise) circulation, a leading warm front and a trailing cold front, plus isobars in hPa. In the Southern Hemisphere circulation would be clockwise, ruling out b and d. Answer c incorrectly places the cold front ahead of the warm front.
explanation.memoryAid: Northern lows spin counter-clockwise: warm front leads, cold front follows — like a clock running backwards.

en.question: For which wind forces is a strong wind warning issued?
answers: Beaufort scale wind force 6 and 7.
Beaufort scale wind force 5 and 6.
Beaufort scale wind force 4 to 5.
Beaufort scale wind force 7 to 8.

explanation.de: Eine Starkwindwarnung wird für Windstärken 6 und 7 auf der Beaufortskala herausgegeben. Ab Windstärke 8 wird eine Sturmwarnung ausgegeben, Windstärken unter 6 rechtfertigen keine Starkwindwarnung.
explanation.en: A strong wind warning (Starkwindwarnung) is issued for wind forces 6 and 7 on the Beaufort scale. Force 8 and above triggers a gale warning (Sturmwarnung), while forces below 6 do not warrant a strong wind warning.
explanation.memoryAid: 6 & 7 = Strong; 8+ = Storm.

en.question: For which wind forces is a storm warning issued?
answers: Wind force 8 or more on the Beaufort scale.
Wind force 6 or more on the Beaufort scale.
Wind force 9 or more on the Beaufort scale.
Wind force 7 or more on the Beaufort scale.

explanation.de: Eine Sturmwarnung wird ab Windstärke 8 Beaufort ausgegeben. Windstärke 7 löst lediglich eine Starkwindwarnung aus, weshalb Antwort d ein häufiger Irrtum ist.
explanation.en: A storm warning is issued when wind force 8 (Beaufort) or higher is forecast. Force 7 triggers a 'strong wind warning' (Starkwindwarnung), not a full storm warning, making option d a common distractor.
explanation.memoryAid: 8 = Gale = Storm Warning: 'Eight is great enough to warn.'

en.question: What is meant by 'fresh wind' (frischer Wind) in official weather reports?
answers: Wind force 5 on the Beaufort scale.
Wind force 4 on the Beaufort scale.
Wind force 6 on the Beaufort scale.
Wind force 7 on the Beaufort scale.

explanation.de: In amtlichen deutschen Wetterberichten entspricht 'frischer Wind' der Windstärke 5 auf der Beaufortskala (17–21 Knoten). Windstärke 4 heißt 'mäßiger Wind', Windstärke 6 'starker Wind' und Windstärke 7 'steifer Wind'.
explanation.en: In official German weather reports, 'fresh wind' (frischer Wind) corresponds to Beaufort force 5 (17–21 knots). Force 4 is 'moderate wind', force 6 is 'strong wind', and force 7 is 'near gale' (steifer Wind).
explanation.memoryAid: Five is Fresh: Beaufort 5 = fresh wind.

en.question: What is meant in official weather reports by "severe storm" (schwerer Sturm), "violent storm" (orkanartiger Sturm), and "hurricane" (Orkan)?
answers: Beaufort scale wind forces 10, 11, and 12.
Beaufort scale wind forces 9, 10, and 11.
Beaufort scale wind forces 11, 12, and 13.
Beaufort scale wind forces 8, 9, and 10.

explanation.de: Auf der Beaufortskala entspricht Windstärke 10 dem 'schweren Sturm', Windstärke 11 dem 'orkanartigen Sturm' und Windstärke 12 dem 'Orkan'. Windstärke 9 ist ein 'Sturm' und Windstärke 8 ein 'stürmischer Wind' – beides niedrigere Kategorien.
explanation.en: On the Beaufort scale, force 10 corresponds to 'severe storm', force 11 to 'violent storm', and force 12 to 'hurricane/orkan'. Force 9 is simply 'storm' and force 8 is 'gale' — both lower categories, making options b and d incorrect.
explanation.memoryAid: 10-11-12: Ten is severe, Eleven is violent, Twelve is the full hurricane.

en.question: How must you adjust your navigation in a fairway in reduced visibility, based on the duty of seamanlike care, when the vessel does not have the technical equipment — in particular for detecting other vessels?
answers: Leave the fairway and, if possible, seek shallow water and anchor. If this is not possible, keep as far to the right as possible within the fairway.
Stop immediately and anchor; if this is not possible, proceed with caution and stay as close as possible in the wake of a vessel ahead.
Continue carefully but briskly so as not to impede other traffic. When hearing fog signals from other vessels, stop and wait, continuously taking soundings.
Keep as far to the right as possible in the fairway and make for the nearest harbour or berth. If in doubt, ask other vessels for their position and correct course.

explanation.de: Ohne technische Ortungsausrüstung (z. B. Radar) muss ein Fahrzeug bei verminderter Sicht das Fahrwasser verlassen und in einem Flachwassergebiet ankern, um eine Kollisionsgefahr mit größeren Fahrzeugen im Fahrwasser zu vermeiden. Ist das Verlassen nicht möglich, ist äußerst rechts zu halten, um die Fahrrinne freizugeben. Antwort b ist falsch, weil sofortiges Ankern im Fahrwasser selbst ebenfalls gefährlich wäre.
explanation.en: Without technical detection equipment (e.g. radar), a vessel in reduced visibility must leave the fairway and anchor in shallow water to avoid collision risk with larger vessels using the channel. If leaving is not possible, keeping as far right as possible is required to keep the main channel clear. Answer b is incorrect because anchoring within the fairway itself would also create a hazard.
explanation.memoryAid: No radar? Get out — leave the fairway, find the shallows, and anchor.

en.question: What is the primary purpose of the Automatic Identification System (AIS)?
answers: Collision avoidance.
Receiving weather data.
Position fixing.
Transmitting nautical warning messages.

explanation.de: AIS dient primär der Kollisionsverhütung, indem es automatisch Schiffskennung, Position, Kurs und Geschwindigkeit an andere Fahrzeuge und Landstationen übermittelt. Dadurch können Verkehr überwacht und potenzielle Gefahrensituationen frühzeitig erkannt werden. Wetterdaten und nautische Warnmeldungen werden über separate Systeme (z. B. Navtex) ausgestrahlt.
explanation.en: AIS primarily serves collision avoidance by automatically broadcasting a vessel's identity, position, course, and speed to other ships and shore stations, allowing traffic to be monitored and potential conflicts identified early. While AIS data can be used to assist with positioning, that is not its primary purpose. Weather data and nautical warnings are transmitted via separate systems (e.g. Navtex).
explanation.memoryAid: AIS = Alert ships to Incoming Ships — it's all about avoiding collisions.

en.question: What information can be exchanged via the Automatic Identification System (AIS)?
answers: Vessel data (static and dynamic), voyage-related data.
Vessel data (static and dynamic), weather data.
Vessel data (static only), voyage-related data.
Vessel data (dynamic only), weather data.

explanation.de: AIS überträgt drei Datenkategorien: statische Schiffsdaten (z. B. MMSI, Schiffsname, Abmessungen), dynamische Schiffsdaten (z. B. Position, Geschwindigkeit, Kurs) sowie reisebezogene Daten (z. B. Reiseziel, ETA, Tiefgang, Ladungsart). Wetterdaten gehören nicht zu den Standard-AIS-Kategorien, weshalb Antworten B und D falsch sind. Antwort C ist falsch, da AIS sowohl statische als auch dynamische Daten umfasst.
explanation.en: AIS transmits three categories of information: static vessel data (e.g. MMSI, vessel name, dimensions), dynamic vessel data (e.g. position, speed, course, heading), and voyage-related data (e.g. destination, ETA, draught, cargo type). Weather data is not a standard AIS data category, making options B and D incorrect. Option C is wrong because AIS includes both static and dynamic data, not just static.
explanation.memoryAid: AIS = Static + Dynamic + Voyage — think 'S-D-V': Ship info, Dynamic position, Voyage details.

en.question: What safety measures must be taken on board, in addition to the rules of conduct prescribed by the Collision Regulations in restricted visibility, based on the duty of seamanlike care?
answers: In particular, use all navigation equipment carefully, increase the visibility of one's own vessel (e.g. radar reflector, AIS), and in an area with shore-based radar advisory service, monitor the radar advisory broadcasts on VHF radio.
In particular, switch on all technical equipment, e.g. radar, AIS, echo sounder, autopilot, and in an area with shore-based radar advisory service, request the radar advisory service on VHF radio.

In particular, use all navigation equipment carefully, increase the visibility of one's own vessel (e.g. radar reflector, AIS), and keep the Vessel Traffic Service (VTS) continuously informed of course and speed.
In particular, switch on all technical equipment, e.g. radar, echo sounder, AIS, autopilot, and keep the Vessel Traffic Service (VTS) continuously informed of course and speed.

explanation.de: Die seemännische Sorgfaltspflicht verlangt bei eingeschränkter Sicht, Navigationsanlagen sorgfältig zu nutzen (nicht nur einzuschalten) und die eigene Sichtbarkeit zu erhöhen (z. B. Radarreflektor, AIS). In Revieren mit Landradarberatung genügt es, die Radarberatung über UKW mitzuhören – eine aktive Anforderung oder ständige Meldepflicht gegenüber der Verkehrszentrale ist nicht vorgeschrieben. Antwort b ist falsch, weil sie das bloße Einschalten betont und eine aktive Anforderung der Radarberatung fordert; Antworten c und d sind falsch, weil eine ständige Kursmeldung an die Verkehrszentrale nicht gefordert ist.
explanation.en: The duty of seamanlike care in restricted visibility requires careful use of navigation equipment (not merely switching it on) and increasing one's own vessel's visibility (e.g. radar reflector, AIS). In areas with a shore-based radar advisory service, it is sufficient to monitor the advisory broadcasts on VHF — actively requesting the service or continuously reporting course and speed to the VTS is not required. Answer b is incorrect because it emphasises simply switching on equipment and demands an active request for radar advisory; answers c and d are incorrect because there is no obligation to continuously report to the VTS.
explanation.memoryAid: Monitor, don't request — listen in to shore radar, and make yourself seen.

en.question: What safety measures must be taken at sea before the onset of heavy weather (strong winds, storm)?
answers: Establish watertight integrity (closed/secured condition), lash down loose items, put on life jackets and keep other rescue equipment ready; if necessary and possible, make for a port of refuge.
Establish watertight integrity (closed/secured condition), lash down loose items, keep life jackets and other rescue equipment ready, prepare distress signalling equipment for use.
Close doors, lash down loose items, keep life jackets and other rescue equipment ready, man radar, helm and VHF.
Close doors, lash down loose items, keep life jackets and other rescue equipment ready, prepare distress signalling equipment for use.

explanation.de: Die richtige Antwort (a) beschreibt den vollständigen Verschlusszustand (nicht nur 'Türen schließen'), das Festzurren loser Gegenstände, das Anlegen der Rettungsweste und – entscheidend – das Anlaufen eines Schutzhafens, wenn möglich. Die anderen Antworten erwähnen das Anlaufen eines Schutzhafens nicht oder verwenden den unvollständigen Begriff 'Türen schließen' statt 'Verschlusszustand herbeiführen'. Seenotsignalmittel vorzubereiten ist erst bei eingetretener Notlage relevant, nicht als vorausschauende Maßnahme vor schwerem Wetter.
explanation.en: The correct answer (a) specifies establishing full watertight/secured integrity (not merely 'closing doors'), lashing down loose items, donning life jackets, and — crucially — seeking a harbour of refuge if necessary and possible. The distractors either omit the harbour-of-refuge option or use the weaker phrase 'close doors' instead of 'establish closed/secured condition'. Preparing distress signals is a reactive measure for an emergency already in progress, not a proactive heavy-weather precaution.
explanation.memoryAid: Before the storm: SEAL (Secure condition), STOW (lash loose items), SUIT UP (life jackets), SHELTER (seek port if possible).

en.question: What equipment can be used to quickly and safely recover a person drifting in the water on board?
answers: Line connection, rescue loop, recovery net, tackle, bathing ladder, main boom.
Line connection, bathing ladder, sea anchor, rescue loop, recovery net, tackle.
Line connection, main boom, anchor chain, tackle, bathing ladder, rescue loop.
Line connection, bathing ladder, lifebuoy, recovery net, main boom, tackle.

explanation.de: Die korrekte Kombination umfasst alle sinnvollen Hilfsmittel zur Bergung einer Person aus dem Wasser: Leinenverbindung (zur Sicherung), Rettungsschlaufe (zum Anlegen um den Körper), Bergenetz (zum Hochziehen), Talje (Flaschenzug als Hebekraft), Badeleiter (zum Klettern) und Großbaum (als Ausleger zum Herausheben). Die anderen Antworten enthalten jeweils ein unpassendes Element: ein Treibanker (b) oder eine Ankerkette (c) dienen nicht der Personenbergung; eine Rettungsboje (d) ist zum Werfen gedacht, nicht zum Aufnehmen.
explanation.en: The correct combination includes all practical aids for recovering a person from the water: a line connection (to secure them), a rescue loop (to place around the body), a recovery net (to haul them up), a tackle (block and tackle for lifting force), a bathing ladder (to climb), and the main boom (as a crane arm for lifting). The other answers each contain an inappropriate item: a sea anchor (b) or anchor chain (c) play no role in person recovery; a lifebuoy (d) is designed for throwing to a casualty, not for hauling them aboard.
explanation.memoryAid: Line → Loop → Net → Tackle → Ladder → Boom: six steps to get someone back on board.

en.question: What should be done if the vessel has capsized?
answers: Stay with the vessel if at all possible and keep the crew together; avoid unnecessary expenditure of energy and attract attention for assistance.
Stay with the vessel if at all possible and send distress signals. Keep the crew together and avoid unnecessary expenditure of energy.
Stay with the vessel if at all possible and mark the accident site; avoid unnecessary expenditure of energy and attract attention for assistance.
Stay with the vessel if at all possible and keep the crew together; recover valuables and the ship's log.

explanation.de: Nach einem Kentern sollte man beim Fahrzeug bleiben, die Besatzung zusammenhalten, Kräfte schonen und auf sich aufmerksam machen. Option b ist ähnlich, aber das aktive Absetzen von Seenotsignalen setzt Ausrüstung voraus, die möglicherweise nicht verfügbar ist; 'Aufmerksamkeit erregen' ist der allgemeinere und korrekte Begriff. Option c nennt das 'Kennzeichnen der Unfallstelle', was keine Priorität ist, und Option d nennt das Bergen von Wertgegenständen, was keine Notfallmaßnahme ist.
explanation.en: After a capsize, the priority is to stay with the vessel, keep the crew together, conserve energy, and attract attention for rescue. Option b is close but specifies sending distress signals, which implies equipment that may not be accessible; 'attract attention' is the correct broader term. Option c incorrectly prioritises marking the accident site, and option d dangerously prioritises recovering valuables over survival.
explanation.memoryAid: Capsize rule: STAY – TOGETHER – SAVE ENERGY – SIGNAL for help.

en.question: How do you prevent persons from falling overboard in heavy seas?
answers: Rig safety lines / jacklines, put on a safety harness and clip in at the designated attachment points.
Rig safety lines / jacklines, muster the crew on deck. Put on life jackets.
Coil up safety lines / jacklines, put on a safety harness and clip into the guardrail.
Muster the crew in the cockpit, put on life jackets, rig safety lines / jacklines.

explanation.de: Die richtige Maßnahme ist: Sicherheitsleinen spannen, Sicherheitsgurt anlegen und an den dafür vorgesehenen Einhakpunkten (nicht an der Reling!) einpicken. Option c ist falsch, weil man Leinen spannt (nicht aufschießt) und die Reling kein geeigneter Einpickpunkt ist. Optionen b und d nennen zwar sinnvolle Elemente, ersetzen aber den Sicherheitsgurt durch das bloße Anlegen von Rettungswesten, was keinen Sturzschutz bietet.
explanation.en: The correct procedure is: rig jacklines, put on a safety harness, and clip in at the designated strong points (not the guardrail). Option c is wrong because you tension lines (not coil them up) and the guardrail is not a proper attachment point. Options b and d mention useful elements but substitute life jackets for harnesses — a life jacket keeps you afloat if you fall in, but does not prevent the fall.
explanation.memoryAid: Jacklines UP, harness ON, clip in RIGHT — in that order.

en.question: Which distress signals may be used?
answers: Rocket flare with red star or red hand flare, continuous sounding of a fog signal device, three flashes or blasts repeated, the word MAYDAY spoken three times by radiotelephone, lateral raising and lowering of arms, flag signal NC, EPIRB, DSC, radar transponder.

Rocket flare with red star or red hand flare, continuous sounding of a fog signal device, three flashes or blasts repeated, sea dye marker, lateral raising and lowering of arms, ball over or under flag signal NC, EPIRB, DSC, radar transponder.

Rocket flare with orange star or orange hand flare, red smoke signal, continuous sounding of a fog signal device, three flashes or blasts repeated, the word MAYDAY spoken three times by radiotelephone, lateral raising and lowering of arms, flag signal NC, EPIRB, DSC, radar transponder.

Rocket flare with red star or red hand flare, continuous sounding of a fog signal device, three flashes or blasts repeated, the word MAYDAY spoken three times by radiotelephone, lateral raising and lowering of arms, flag signal NC, EPIRB, DSC, radar transponder.

explanation.de: Laut COLREG Anlage IV sind die offiziellen Notsignale u.a. rote Leuchtraketen oder rote Handfackeln, anhaltendes Nebelsignal, SOS per Licht/Ton, dreimal MAYDAY per Funk, seitliches Armschwingen, Flaggensignal NC, EPIRB, DSC und Radartransponder. Antwort (b) enthält fehlerhafte Elemente (Seewasserfärber und 'Ball über/unter NC'), und Antwort (c) nennt fälschlicherweise orange statt rote Signale. Antwort (a) und (d) sind identisch und korrekt.
explanation.en: According to COLREG Annex IV, the recognised distress signals include red rocket flares or red hand flares, continuous fog signals, SOS by light or sound, MAYDAY three times by radiotelephony, lateral arm waving, flag signal NC, EPIRB, DSC, and radar transponder. Answer (b) incorrectly includes a sea dye marker and a ball above/below NC, which are not in this combination. Answer (c) incorrectly states orange instead of red signals.
explanation.memoryAid: Distress = RED: red flares, red flag signal NC — orange and dye markers are NOT part of this standard COLREG list.

en.question: What does the flag signal "NC" on a vessel mean?
answers: Vessel in distress.
Vessel in public service.
Vessel carrying dangerous goods.
Vessel leaving berth.

explanation.de: Das Flaggensignal "NC" aus dem Internationalen Signalbuch bedeutet "Ich bin in Seenot und benötige sofortige Hilfe". Es ist eines der offiziellen Notzeichen nach den COLREG. Die anderen Antworten beschreiben keine anerkannten Bedeutungen dieses Signals.
explanation.en: The flag signal "NC" from the International Code of Signals means "I am in distress and require immediate assistance". It is one of the official distress signals under COLREG. The other answers do not correspond to any recognised meaning of this signal.
explanation.memoryAid: NC = 'Need Care' (distress signal).

en.question: What does the continuous sounding of a fog signal device from a vessel mean?
answers: Vessel in distress.
Vessel carrying dangerous goods.
Keep-away signal.
Attention signal.

explanation.de: Das anhaltende Ertönen eines Nebelsignalgerätes ist ein international anerkanntes Notsignal, das anzeigt, dass sich das Fahrzeug in Seenot befindet und Hilfe benötigt. Es darf nicht mit regulären Nebelsignalen (die festgelegte Kurz-/Langtonmuster verwenden) oder dem Bleib-weg-Signal verwechselt werden.
explanation.en: A continuous sounding of a fog signal device is an internationally recognised distress signal, indicating that the vessel is in distress and requires assistance. It should not be confused with regular fog signals (which use defined short/long blast patterns) or the keep-away signal (used near certain hazardous vessels).
explanation.memoryAid: Continuous = Crisis — a non-stop horn means the vessel needs help NOW.

en.question: What does the following Morse signal, given by light or sound, mean?
answers: Distress signal.
Fog signal.
Keep-away signal.
Overtaking signal.

explanation.de: Das Morsesignal SOS (· · · — — — · · ·) ist das international anerkannte Seenotsignal. Es wird sowohl als Lichtsignal (z. B. mit einer Lampe) als auch als Schallsignal gegeben und bedeutet, dass ein Fahrzeug in schwerer Not ist und sofortige Hilfe benötigt. Nebelsignale, Bleib-weg-Signale und Überholsignale haben andere, festgelegte Formen.
explanation.en: The Morse signal SOS (· · · — — — · · ·) is the internationally recognised distress signal. It can be given by light (e.g. a lamp) or by sound and indicates that a vessel is in grave danger and requires immediate assistance. Fog signals, keep-away signals, and overtaking signals each have their own distinct, defined forms.
explanation.memoryAid: SOS: Save Our Souls — three dots, three dashes, three dots.

en.question: What does a rocket with a red star signal mean?
answers: Distress at sea.
Request to stop.
Firing exercise.
Request to alter course.

explanation.de: Eine Leuchtrakete mit einem roten Stern ist ein international anerkanntes Notsignal und zeigt einen Seenotfall an. Die anderen Antworten beschreiben keine Bedeutungen dieses Signals — Schießübungen oder Kursänderungsaufforderungen werden durch andere Signalmittel kommuniziert.
explanation.en: A rocket with a red star is an internationally recognized distress signal indicating an emergency at sea. The other options do not correspond to this signal — firing exercises or requests to alter course are communicated by different means.
explanation.memoryAid: Red star rocket = RED ALERT: someone needs rescue!

en.question: What does the following flag signal mean?
answers: Vessel in distress.
Vessel in public service.
Vessel carrying dangerous goods.
Vessel leaving berth.

explanation.de: Das gezeigte Flaggensignal ist das internationale Codesignal NC, das weltweit bedeutet: 'Ich bin in Seenot und benötige sofortige Hilfe.' Es ist eines der anerkannten Notsignale gemäß COLREG Anlage IV. Die anderen Antworten beschreiben völlig andere Situationen mit anderen Signalen oder Kennzeichnungen.
explanation.en: The signal shown is the International Code flag signal NC, which universally means 'I am in distress and require immediate assistance.' It is one of the recognized distress signals under COLREG Annex IV. The other options describe entirely different situations that use different signals or markings.
explanation.memoryAid: NC = 'Need Care' — a vessel flying NC needs immediate help.

en.question: What does one of the following signals on a vessel mean?
answers: Vessel in distress.
Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.
Vessel carrying dangerous goods.
Vessel at anchor with a length of more than 100 m.

explanation.de: Die im Katalog referenzierten Signale (z. B. rote Raketen, Flagge N über C, oranger Rauch, MAYDAY-Ruf) sind international anerkannte Notsignale gemäß Anlage IV der KVR (COLREG). Sie zeigen an, dass ein Fahrzeug in Seenot ist und Hilfe benötigt. Manövrierbehinderte Fahrzeuge oder Fahrzeuge mit gefährlichen Gütern haben andere, klar definierte Signale.
explanation.en: The signals referenced in this catalogue question (e.g. red rockets, N-over-C flag, orange smoke, MAYDAY call) are internationally recognised distress signals as listed in Annex IV of the COLREG. They indicate that a vessel is in distress and requires assistance. Vessels restricted in their ability to manoeuvre, or those carrying dangerous goods, use entirely different, separately defined signals.
explanation.memoryAid: Red rocket or N/C flag = Need help — distress, not just danger.
